0.title: Prologue — Before the Clock Started
0.content: Before there was a countdown, there was a tidal wave. It began with a tidal wave. The party washed ashore from Gamble Island, half-drowned and a long way from anywhere, into the town of Saki — where they put down a nest of cultists and a demon before they’d even caught their breath. In Saki they crossed paths with Baz Stricknaz: bastard prince of Jun, host to a Reaper, and a smiling recruiter looking for blades to add to his cause. The alliance was brief. When it soured, the party turned on him — and Bram put a knife to his throat. Baz died, and as he died he cursed. The Reaper woke, Baz’s shadow swallowed his own corpse, and what rose from it was a ghost-and-reaper hybrid consumed by rage. From that moment on, Baz has hunted Bram through the party’s shadows, relentless and patient. He only needs to catch him once. Baz’s people outlived him. His half-siblings Willamet and Priscilla Adhmad, clerics who had wanted the ritual stopped as badly as anyone; Willamet’s bodyguard Mark; the spies Blade and Silrael; and six Junish soldiers all came with the party when it left Saki. Saki’s mayor had “perished in the battle,” and a man named Munyon, who had spent it saving townsfolk alongside the town’s mages, appointed himself the new one. His riders would join the muster later.

1.title: The siege of Wip
1.content: The party traveled inland to Wip with Baz’s people in tow and found the city already taken. Newport had sailed around the continent and come in from the north, and clockwork igloids under the commanders of the Melts family held every district but one: the fortress called The Rock, which had never been breached and was not going to start now. What followed was the longest single stretch of the First Run. The three factions of the city’s Thieves Guild. A Rakshasa called Caspian, and the mage he took. The rescue of Luna Cantine. A gnome in a gun foundry who said he was Rat’s mentor. The fortress, the lab beneath it, a drill the size of a district, a drow spymaster with her own war, and a queen. It is told in two chapters: . → 2.2: The Road to Wip — three days of training, two souls sold, and a city that had already fallen. → 2.3: The Rock — the fortress, the crystal, and the face R4 still wears. It cost them. Ralf died in the Soul of the Rock and came back in an igloid body with Ley Crystal shards for eyes and his own hat on top. Emma Wip was murdered by the thing wearing Catroniel’s face. And in the chaos, R4 stepped into the dead ruler’s place, taking the reins of Wip’s government behind a borrowed face.

2.title: The clock starts ticking
2.content: Then came Jun, and the Battle of the Ziggurat. Heart Melts — a clockwork dragon — crashed down through the temple floor and into the ziggurat below, and there he destroyed the Jun Ley Crystal. The barrier that had sealed that city against the dark went dark itself, and aberrant things spilled through. The gods had built their wall out of crystal. Now one of its stones was shattered. Only the Wip Ley Crystal still held — and by every reckoning it had roughly five years of power left before Ghroth’s path to the world opened. The doomsday clock had started ticking. They killed him for it, at the Battle of the Jun Ziggurat. It did not put the crystal back. → 2.4: The Dream and the Long Preparation — the night the gods came to explain what they wanted.

4.title: The Road to Wip
4.content: Three days of training, two souls sold, one city already lost. They left Saki with more company than they had arrived with: Willamet and Priscilla Adhmad, clerics and half-siblings to the man the party had just killed; Mark, who goes where Willamet goes; the spies Blade and Silrael; six Junish soldiers; and Alissa the mage, who had the plan. The plan was Baz’s plan with the human sacrifice taken out of it. Go to Wip, spend the King’s seal on magic items from Alissa’s contact, teleport to Jun, defend it. Everyone agreed it was a good plan. It was three days to Wip.

5.title: Three days of training
5.content: They used the road. Mark taught Asfache and Steven to parry; the clerics gave Smolder, Ralf and Bram a free spell a day each; Una studied with Alissa; and Blade and Silrael taught Rat how to hurt people who were not looking. The road repaid the effort by trying to kill them roughly once a day. A kettle of migrating giant eagles came down on the column. A family with a broken cart axle came the other way with the first real news anyone had: Wip has been invaded. Then two glabrezus. Then two bone devils and six hellhounds, which is where the trip stopped being funny. The devils offered safe passage in exchange for souls. Steven sold his. Ralf sold two. Nobody made him. Ralf simply had more on hand than the others and saw no reason to leave a bargaining position unexploited. The party walked on unharmed and did not discuss it at length, which is a habit they have never broken. Safe passage, priced in souls. Ralf paid double and has never explained why.

6.title: Goblins, WonderWads, and one exploding cart
6.content: After the devils came a strange little man named Tingle, who sold them maps of Junkweil, the world, and — repeatedly useful thereafter — the city of Wip, sewers included. Then two hundred goblin raiders out of the Vale ambushed them, and the party killed a hundred and forty-two and put the bodies in the bag of holding, because Steven wanted them. Somewhere in there a merchant handed out free samples of WonderWads, which make you more charming. Everyone tried one. Ralf and Bram got hooked, and neither of them knew it — the party spent months noticing those two were slow off the mark in a fight and being unable to say why. Then the traveling potion salesman they had wronged in a previous life came back for revenge. Una put him to sleep, somebody lifted a potion off his cart, and the Glyph of Warding on it detonated the entire inventory. Una’s tongue exploded. Asfache was teleported onto a stack of orange crates. Every woman present acquired cat eyes. Priscilla’s clothes changed color every time she cast a spell. They arrived at Wip in that condition.

7.title: The silent city
7.content: Glassplace was empty. Not evacuated — silent. Doors shut, streets clean, nobody in them. Ralf turned Rat and Smolder invisible and put them in the air, and the shape of it came clear: Newport had sailed around the continent and taken the city from the north. Fishsong was thriving, its crowds listening to evangelists promise that under Lady Prodigy Melts they would be richer than ever — free WonderWads daily, an igloid for every family’s heavy lifting, a safe and better Wip — and offering a reward for anything useful about how to get inside The Rock. The Rock itself was ringed by igloids under a large man in a crown, Pyre Melts, with drones roped up its sheer sides swinging hammers. The Ghostforge was buried in fog that leaked blasts, flashes and the occasional scream. The Harbour was Newport war galleys, Westgate was igloids hauling the nobles’ furniture down to them, and Moongate was garrisoned. And out in Traders Bay sat a minotaur ship, riding at anchor, waiting patiently to learn who it would be trading with.

8.title: Under the Glassplace
8.content: The company split. Priscilla, Blade and Silrael were flown invisibly in to find the Thieves Guild. Willamet, Mark and four soldiers went to Moongate, which went badly and would cost them. On the ground, the party realized they were being watched by children. Una made friends with one — a halfling girl named Lyla — who showed them the way down into the underground city beneath Glassplace. There they met Liam, who wanted proof of who they were and knew where to get it: Otto the 7th, Bram’s brother, left behind by the same parents in the same way. The brothers performed their famous knives act. Asfache won silver arm-wrestling. Smolder and Rat held a pickpocketing contest that Rat won and Smolder cheated at the end of, so it would look like he hadn’t. Both of them know what they know. Liam sold them the underground river and the sewer entrances for coin, a club, and every orange Asfache owned.

9.title: Stinky
9.content: The river ran ten feet wide and waist deep in the dark. Steven jumped in first. It turns out Steven is a phenomenal swimmer. Rat walked into a giant snake. Asfache fed it WonderWads, noticed it was guarding a clutch of eggs, and got everyone past without a scratch. He named it Stinky. Smolder gave serious, extended thought to stealing an egg and — this is worth recording — did not. Further on the stalactites dropped on them. Darkmantles, swarming, wrapping heads in magical darkness, with giant centipedes coming up the tunnel behind. Una cleaned the water with a cantrip so they could see what was biting their legs. Smolder netted one, skewered several more, and kept one as a hat, to mirror Ralf’s. The underground river. Smolder kept one as a hat.

10.title: The DwarvoDraco
10.content: Then Steven went for a swim. He had spotted alligators, and the alligators liked him, so he went deeper — and found a tunnel with a stone lizard head carved above it. The symbol of Essyliss. Behind it was a mushroom-lit cavern and ten lizardfolk who worship her, farming glowing fungus and stealing the occasional crate of fruit from the neighbors without ever hurting anyone. Steven joined their prayer — “I’m a lizard” — and their elder, Aussssten, asked him one question: are you traveling with a dwarf? . He was. He fetched the party, and when Aussssten saw Ralf beside him in a wizard hat riddled with stars, that settled it. On the cavern wall was a mural: a lizard head wearing a nose ring, and above it a dwarf surrounded by stars. Steven was the DwarvoDraco — he who walks with dwarves — and had apparently been so for some time before anybody thought to mention it. Aussssten gave him the Everscale — the totem of the chosen of Essyliss, which lets its bearer put a point of magic into anything they make with their own hands, once every six days. And wielded by the DwarvoDraco, said Aussssten, it is what restores Essyliss to the power she held before the great destruction. Ralf and Smolder spent the next hour agreeing that Steven had absolutely not told them everything, and that these lizard people were ridiculous. They were right about the first part. They have been wrong about the second ever since.

11.title: “Those are my fighters!”
11.content: The sewers surfaced through a grate into a fighting arena — the headquarters of the Wip Thieves Guild. Smolder went up first and was met by Dryzzlazz Dig’Rodar, the Spider Queen, a drow drider, who asked whether they had anyone to vouch for them and started dropping her children on them when they didn’t. Priscilla, from the crowd: “STOP! Those are my fighters!” Dryzzlazz took it in stride and asked who was fighting today. Asfache volunteered, then raised the stakes to a death match, which the crowd loved. He won brutally, looked to Ralf for a ruling on whether to finish it, got one, and finished it. Afterward he made friends with Skoll Cantine, son of the matriarch of the Wolves, and his wolf Lucas. Una learned the leader of the Moles was missing and something had gone wrong in the Ghostforge, and Bram quietly handed Smolder a token and a letter he had lifted during a reverse heist with Otto.

12.title: The Big Meet
12.content: Three heads run the Guild: the Spiders (Dryzzlazz), the Wolves (the Cantines, Skoll speaking), and the Moles — Aegor, who did not attend and was never going to. The news at the table was ugly. Willamet had been captured, having opened his mouth in Moongate, and the Cantines meant to trade him to Newport for their kidnapped matriarch, Luna Cantine. Skoll’s terms were simple: rescue his mother before the trade, and he would hand Willamet back. Then Smolder “happened” to find a third token. Dryzzlazz dropped it in the Ghostblood chalice, which confirmed what had become of Aegor and expanded a sixty-foot Zone of Truth over the meeting. What followed was a masterclass in telling the truth without saying anything, capped by Rat performing a piece of sleight of hand that duplicated a ten-thousand-gold writ of Jun in front of a room full of professional thieves. The deal: passage to the Harbour, in exchange for solving the Ghostforge problem, protecting the prisoner exchange, and ten thousand gold. Priscilla paid half up front. Dryzzlazz passed the writ to Skoll and told him to cash it quickly — the things were getting harder and harder to cash. Afterward Rat got a hand on Dryzzlazz and spoke to her in touch-based thieves’ cant. She was being controlled by arachnomancers, she told him, who kept her true and insane personality suppressed, and who meant to steal guns and take them down to the drow.

13.title: The Harbour
13.content: The Guild moved them by sewer toward the shortest crossing, at Shady Lane. They were caught anyway, brawled with igloids, started losing, and escaped underground on a distraction improvised by Priscilla and Alissa. So they rode the underground river instead, surfaced in the bay, and Rat and Smolder set Newport ships alight as a distraction. By the light of the burning galleys they crossed the rooftops to the Giddyup Saloon, where Alissa finally admitted what her contact was. She had signed a contract with a fiend: information from her, magic items for her allies, a Ring of Mass Teleport for herself. Inside, two men flanked a four-foot mirror. A voice welcomed her and told her to take her ring and look into it. She looked into it, went white, and was gone. The Giddyup Saloon. Alissa looked into the mirror, and was gone.

14.title: Caspian
14.content: The mirror’s owner introduced himself as Caspian. He was a rakshasa, he was unhurried, and he had no intention of giving her back — he needed a student of the Arcane University to open the enclave at Mont Kiara, and Alissa was one. They attuned their new gear and went back in. Smolder, in his Robe of Eyes, listened in while Caspian met Prodigy Melts and traded 150 igloids for the Magic Bomb spell and whatever he could learn about the Ghostforge. Prodigy mentioned an exchange she had to make later that day; she thought it might get her the key to Jun. Meanwhile Rat took three thousand gold in gems and coin out of the building, and then found a bag with a thousand more in platinum. Confronting Caspian got them nowhere — he would simply planeshift away if pressed — but he let them speak to Alissa through the glass. She blurted out the location and passphrase of the enclave, believing it discharged her contract, and Caspian pointed out, pleasantly, that the wording was give me what I need to reach the enclave, and only a student’s hand would do that. So Alissa made her own terms: she would go with him, if he gave the party a Ring of Mass Teleport. And she made them swear they would save Jun.

15.title: Luna, and the bite
15.content: Smolder’s eavesdropping had also produced Luna Cantine’s location: a ship in the harbour called the Gentle Perfection. Rat ran the extraction, and it was clean. They teleported into the Thieves Guild with the matriarch of the Wolves in tow, hours before Newport expected to be handed her. Skoll returned Willamet to Priscilla on the spot, granted free passage through Moongate, and offered Asfache the bite. He took it, and the Cantines made him a lycanthrope. Luna gave them the one thing the Guild had never managed to buy: if you want the ghosts out of the Ghostforge, the answer is at the Heartforge.

16.title: The Ghostforge
16.content: They teleported into fog. Igloids and freed ghosts were fighting each other in it. They fought ghosts, chased down a gnome named Gandor, and then a teenage human burst into the room, cracked his voice, tripped, and farted. This was Perception Melts, and he was delighted to meet them, and he believed every word when they told him they were ghostbusters from NDC. He offered three thousand gold for a clean removal. The next day he and Prodigy turned up ready to storm the district alongside them, and Una talked them out of it on the grounds that professionals work alone. Prodigy left saying she would like a word with Smolder later, about their mutual friend. Gandor took them to the Heartforge, and in the Heartforge was a gun manufacturing line, and at the head of it was a gnome with an artificial arm and leg. Catroniel. Cat. Rat’s long-lost mentor. It was a very big moment. Cat had killed Aegor and had been building guns in secret with his crew, the Ghostbloods — gnomes, dwarves, and his lieutenant Carxi. His ambition was straightforward and enormous: take the third seat on the Guild, unite the factions, smuggle a force into The Rock, take it, and throw Newport out of Wip. He also knew about a minotaur smuggling operation running guns from Gaiadon into The Rock, and when. The party told him Tamsend came first. Cat said he would meet the Guild without them.

17.title: Meanwhile, Bram
17.content: Bram and Otto had been separated from the party at the saloon, and spent four days having an entirely different campaign. They fled into the alleys, got lost, and pulled a gnome woman in black out of the hands of igloid brawlers — Carxi, who knew the city and had a rowboat. They rowed for the Ghostforge shore under fire and were saved by a minotaur ship out of Gaiadon, whose crew Bram talked into letting them perform. From that performance he learned about a shipment of power armor and guns going into The Rock in four days, and the meeting point: an ash tree in Cleargate Fields. Then he imitated the captain’s voice well enough to get a grunt to hand over the passphrase — “Rock Strong Keepers Brave” — and told nobody, because it was the only thing he had to bargain with. Carxi took them to Catroniel, who was unimpressed by the withholding and visibly respected it anyway. The brothers helped run a trial of the smuggling route and were paid in exactly one gun. Then Bram spotted someone in the bushes and pulled out Lord Franklin Wherebethal, a merchant hiding in the woods, who took them to Farmans Grotto — a secret hollow full of Wip’s displaced nobility. Two nights of entertaining nobles bought them the state of the city and Sammy, a dwarf leader out of Cleargate who offered fighters in exchange for weapons. On the fourth day they collected their pistols, five bullets apiece, ammunition made of platinum. Then they led Cat, Carxi and a squad of Ghostbloods through the sewers to the arena — because the Guild had told Cat to prove himself by finding it, and the Ash brothers were the only people he had who already knew where it was.

18.title: Mont Kiara
18.content: Cat’s meeting worked. He became the third head of the Thieves Guild. The party missed it. They were at Tamsend Arcane University, following Ralf’s lead, which meant visitor passes and a call on his old conjuration professor, Dr. Fando Elzir. They bought an owlbear mascot plushie at the gift shop on Ralf’s tab, drank experimental potions in Research and Development, bought scrolls, and paid for a teleport to Mont Kiara — which put them on the summit, which is the wrong end of the mountain. Ralf got them down with Tenser’s Floating Disk and Feather Fall, faked moonlight with an illusion so the door would open, and sent Merlin ahead as bait. At the far end of the enclave they found Caspian, and beside him a silent, blank-faced Alissa under his control. Rat and Steven put her down without hurting her, and Rat lifted the seal for the writs off her while she was out. Then Asfache killed Caspian with one enormous, pent-up critical hit. They swept every paper in the room into a bag — including an incomplete Magic Bomb spell — picked up Alissa, put on her Ring of Mass Teleport, and went home to a sewer in Wip, where they made a hut and laughed until they couldn’t breathe. Cat was meeting the Thieves Guild that evening. He had a plan for The Rock, and he wanted Rat to run part of it. → 2.3: The Rock — a fortress that had never been breached, and everyone in the city with a plan to be inside it.

20.title: Farylse & the Chronologians
20.content: Time cops, a deal struck under duress, and a shattered plane where time is terrain. You do not simply rewind five years of history without someone noticing. The party’s jump was intercepted by the Chronologians — time cops, guardians of the timeline’s integrity. They fought their way through a Chronologian stronghold alongside Mordenkainen, freed Freya from captivity, and came at last before the Chronologians’ leader: Damian Heath. The stronghold, as negotiated by Steven.

21.title: The deal
21.content: Damian did not want to stop them. He wanted to use them. The terms were simple. He would release the party and Freya to go and defeat Ghroth. If they succeeded, he would recruit them to upset the balance of power within the Council of Eternity — the mysterious body that governs time itself. If they failed, they would die, and Damian would remain steward of a timeline already doomed to fall. He had nothing to lose by letting them try. The party took the deal.

22.title: The shattered plane
22.content: Beyond Damian’s stronghold lay Farylse — a broken temporal plane where time isn’t a current you drift along but terrain you can climb, cross, and fall off of. The party spent what felt like a long while there, and met strange company: . | the Unnumbered, exiles of the Land of Gears, cut off from their hive-mind when their king abandoned them; | the Void, and the Weavers who work the loom of time; | Captain Jhodos Rumoxath, a triton pirate king who gave everything to save his crew, and who taught the party to command Farylse’s temporal terrain; | a colossal Giant Robot washed ashore with a skeleton inside it; | and a crazed, long-haired woman in a crown, endlessly guarding a portal that led nowhere anyone could name. | . The Land of Gears — a city on turning cog-plates, and the home the Unnumbered were cut loose from. The Giant Robot, run aground and going green. Somebody had been inside it, and had not got out. Not everything in Farylse wanted to teach them anything. The spider queen, for one. And the Void, which is a place, and also — occasionally, and unpleasantly — a thing that comes out of it.

23.title: The things that live there
23.content: Not everything on Farylse was a monster. Some of what watched the gates had been people, once — people who made a deal with Damian Heath or with Astridia, and now keep the doors they bargained for. Shatter. The gear-people’s souls, caught in time and still working. Each one is many of them at once, and they have never stopped digging. Gloom. The immortal general of the City of the Palanquin, who carried a city and an army out of Ghroth’s path and then watched all of it turn into the other things on this page. Astridia offered to numb it if he would guard her portal. The party left with his Captain’s Seal. Regret. Farylse’s name for Captain Jhodos Rumoxath, the triton pirate king who lost his crew and never once put it down. He taught the party to ride the time-terrain and gave them his Star-Shell Pendant. They learned to manipulate the time-terrain, banking decades of it for later. And they tied up a loose end from the First Run: the White Lion had survived their ambush — Artists cannot truly be killed — and here he was again. The party returned his severed body parts (still tucked in their bags of holding) in exchange for a fresh writ to silence the Siren Song and two leonin followers, Nala and Raja. When at last the way home opened, the party stepped through it knowing one hard rule: they can never return to Farylse. Whatever they carried out — items, allies, knowledge, the writ — was all they would ever get from that place. → Chapter 4: The Second Run Begins — the same five years, played with foreknowledge.

25.title: The Rock
25.content: A fortress that had never been breached, and four separate people with a plan to own it. Back in the sewers, everyone came to the table: Cat and the Ghostbloods, Dryzzlazz and the Spiders, Luna and Skoll Cantine for the Wolves, Priscilla, Willamet, Blade, Silrael, and the party. Catroniel had won the third seat, and he used it immediately. His plan, laid out plainly: get inside The Rock, empty its armory, arm the Guild and the Tinkers with what came out plus the guns from the Heartforge, and then drive Newport out of Wip en masse. He offered guns to the Cantines and the Spiders for their support, and asked for safe passage through the sewers. He said he had further plans he would share once they were inside. What he needed was somebody to relieve the minotaur smugglers of their cargo and walk into The Rock wearing their reputation. Everyone in the room turned and looked at the party.

26.title: The note
26.content: Cat took Rat aside more than once, and not everything he said was for the table. He wanted an igloid captured for study. He wanted the layout of The Rock — how the security worked, where the armory was, what the guard looked like from the inside. He wanted Rat to be ready for a coup. And he wanted Rat to carry a note to whoever was commanding Newport at the negotiations, offering to accept Newport’s supremacy over the region so long as Cat was the one ruling Wip, with trade terms and shared gun technology attached. Rat took the instructions. He had known Cat since he was a child. There was no reason on earth to doubt him.

27.title: Into the crates
27.content: They met the minotaur contact Thum’gad and talked their way into the shipment by hiding inside the crates. Bram spotted the ambush a moment before it landed, and Smolder noticed something else entirely: the Wip officer running the exchange was being scried on. Newport igloids came out of the treeline in force, and the fight went badly enough that the party detonated an entire crate of guns to buy themselves an exit. Rat, still inside a crate at the time, shoveled everything that hadn’t exploded into the bag of holding. Then a running fight through the forest — gunfire, soldiers, potholes, and a stampede of thoroughly spooked deer — with three surviving Rock soldiers named Jared, Thomas and Steve running beside them. The run for the secret entrance. Two of the three soldiers did not make it.

28.title: Pyre at the door
28.content: At the secret entrance stood a red-haired man in a crown — Pyre Melts, eldest of the Melts children — beside a robed wizard named Vanthal Reminar, with a platoon waiting in the trees. Una talked them into walking away from the door. The moment they were far enough out, the ruse frayed, Ralf gave the signal, the soldiers tackled Pyre and Vanthal, and Una convinced the surrounding troops that the two tacklers were the real threat. Smolder took Pyre’s golden crown of rubies off his head on the way past. Everyone ran. Jared was burned to death. Thomas was disintegrated. Steve and the party made the tunnel and sealed it behind them, and the door held. Una noticed, going in, that her magic felt muffled — the closer to The Rock, the quieter it got.

29.title: Emma Wip
29.content: The tunnel ran to a translucent purple wall with a brass horn set into it. On the far side stood a tall woman in a silver crown of welded emeralds, flanked by ten hulking figures in runed stone armor. Emma Wip knew Steve by name. He told her what had happened at the ash tree — an ambush, a rearguard, a crate of guns going up — and Emma took the news standing. Then she asked who these people were, why they had helped him, and how many guns they had actually recovered. They answered all three, and she let them in. The war room was worse than the view from outside. The Rock held five thousand soldiers. Newport had five thousand men and more than fifteen thousand igloids, with five manufacturing facilities in the city turning out five hundred a day. So the party spread out what they had. Connections in the Thieves Guild. The Cantines and their wolves. And a spell called La Bomba — half of it, taken off a dead rakshasa’s desk. Emma gave them the laboratory in the Soul of the Rock, and the wizard Ragar Huntsfellow to work with. And she gave Cat a seat on her council as Master of War.

30.title: Nine hundred missiles
30.content: Ralf, Una and Smolder worked the lab with Ragar and took La Bomba apart. It runs in three steps: build a receptacle orb, channel magic missiles into it over hours and days, then let the whole accumulated weight of it out at once. The receptacle’s material decides how much it can hold. Precious gems will take a hundred and five missiles. A fragment of the Soul of the Rock — the city’s own Ley Crystal, sitting a room away — will take nine hundred. That number has been in the party’s head ever since. Meanwhile Asfache, Rat and Steven paraglided off The Rock into the city to keep the Guild sweet, and found out on arrival that Dryzzlazz’s arachnomancer handlers had abandoned her in the arena, and that the Spider Queen had gone back to being exactly as insane as she was before they got hold of her. And in Ragar’s workshop, the party met one of his inventions: a warforged artificer, freshly awake, designated R41F.

31.title: The drill
31.content: Newport answered with a machine. A Spider Drill — colossal, mechanical, three enormous bits grinding into the flank of The Rock, a cannon slung under its belly and repeating scatter guns bolted over every surface. A scouting team went out and confirmed the worst of it, including the timeline. It would be through the purple barrier in roughly twelve hours, and nobody knew how long the barrier would hold once it was touched. Twelve hours to finish La Bomba. Emma, out of options, sent her Spymaster down to the lab to help.

32.title: Etheniss
32.content: Etheniss Orlytlar was a drow, and she had spent the siege quietly waiting for a reason to be in that room. She helped. She genuinely helped. And while she helped she walked the chamber placing books, one at a time, all around the Ley Crystal — every one of them rigged with a Glyph of Warding. When the receptacle was filled she offered a toast, and the wine carried drow poison. Alissa was killed by her death lance. Smolder saw the books for what they were, gathered every one of them up, and threw them into the furnace — which was the only thing to do with them and also detonated the entire set at once. The blast wrecked Ragar’s machines, damaged the Soul of the Rock, and immolated Ralf. They killed Etheniss for it. Her purpose came out afterward, and it had never had anything to do with Newport: she was weakening the crystal to weaken the Underwell — the ancient seal, powered by the Soul of the Rock, that keeps the drow beneath the world from reaching the top of it. She got what she wanted. Both the purple barrier and the Underwell were left leaking. The Soul of the Rock. Smolder did the only thing you can do with a stack of rigged books, and it killed Ralf.

33.title: The hat
33.content: Afterward, in the wreckage, Ralf’s wizard hat was found intact. Ragar had an igloid head on his bench. Smolder put the hat on it and pushed Ley Crystal shards into the eye sockets. Ralf came back.

34.title: The Underwell
34.content: Below, the drow massed against a seal that no longer sealed. A priestess called up through the gap and announced that she had ten thousand troops standing ready to help the humans with their war, and asked, sweetly, why the barrier was only weakened and not fully down. She had, she said, heard from Etheniss. Emma gave the party the choice: the threat above, or the threat below. They went down. Mason Wip escorted them, and Captain Othelstan held the chamber, and the drow came up in waves — warriors on giant spiders, a mage riding a carrion crawler, and finally a fire giant climbing out of the hole. The party fought to get the cover onto the well while the well kept producing reasons not to. Mason Wip was killed. Othelstan died, and stayed dead. Rat got the cover closed. Then the forge crews arrived, hauling a massive iron forge cover to weigh the seal down for good — and behind them came three drow the party recognized from the Thieves Guild, dressed as cryptkeepers, carrying a map of The Rock’s secret tunnels and a note from Etheniss in Undercommon.

35.title: Otto
35.content: Above, through all of it, Bram and Otto had been flying a carpet over the battle for the city, dodging gunfire and harpoons and doing what the Ash brothers do. A harpoon caught Otto and pulled him off it. Bram went looking. He found his brother being tortured by Pyre Melts, who wanted to know where his crown had gone, and who killed him for not knowing. Bram got out, and mourned alone, and came back to the war room the next day and sang the battle for the people who had won it. They named him the aerial savior of Wip. He did not tell them what the flight had cost him for a while.

36.title: The whistle
36.content: In the aftermath the numbers came in, and for once they were good: of the five igloid manufacturing facilities in the city, four had been destroyed. Emma had also captured a Newport figure named Donny, and intended to trade him back to the Melts family for their withdrawal from Wip. When the Rock Guard seized him, something small fell out of his pocket and rang on the stone. It was a whistle to Gamble Island.

37.title: Ancient Gamble Island
37.content: At the meeting, Pyre Melts made his own offer: ancient combat, to the death, over the crown Smolder had stolen off his head. Otherwise the siege continued. Then Freya took a pair of temporal scissors to the moment, and the party landed on Gamble Island a very long time before there was anything on it. A port. A shack. Nothing else. Inside the shack, a small man was dealing blackjack. They played, they asked questions, and they won a favor and a prize: a painting of an ear. This was the party’s first meeting with Flamencio, though he would not think of it that way when they met him again. Then the Chronologians arrived — the time cops, for the first time, and none of the party had the faintest idea what they were looking at. Flamencio sent everybody home before it could escalate, having first been bribed with the transfer of Asfache’s smoothie business. Ancient Gamble Island. The prize was a painting of an ear. The men in the doorway were the time cops.

38.title: The war room
38.content: They came back to a strangely empty Rock. The attendants were gone. Carxi met them and explained that everyone was preparing a celebration in the grand hall, and that the council was waiting for them in the war room. Cat’s ambush was waiting in the war room. Smolder killed Priscilla in the chaos. Cat killed Emma Wip — and then changed shape. It had never been Catroniel. Not in the Heartforge, not at the Guild table, not in any of the quiet conversations with Rat. Every instruction Rat had been given, every map he had drawn, had been drawn for a thing wearing his mentor’s face. Rat was turned to stone, briefly. A stranger named Alamil appeared in the middle of it, for reasons nobody understood at the time. And then the party killed the creature, and stood in a room with a dead queen in it.

39.title: The face
39.content: R4 picked up Emma’s crown and put it on. He took her face with it. The crown that runs the purple barrier, the crown the Wip family has worn for generations, went onto a warforged who had been awake for about a week — and Wip has been ruled by a dead woman ever since. The rest of the room moved just as fast. Luna Cantine got her family onto the council of Wip, and got R4’s approval for a discreet arrangement: Gemma and Peter Wip would be sent by ship to negotiate an alliance, and that ship would be attacked by pirates. Steven got Aussssten onto the council too, with Luna’s blessing, and the lizardfolk under the Glassplace acquired a protector at the top of the city. And Rat heard voices for the first time. Several of them, overlapping, each claiming him. Then one underneath the others, deeper than the rest: . “No — he is mine.” . The party started calling him Dark Rat, and did not laugh very much when they said it.

40.title: The first council
40.content: R4 convened his first council meeting as the ruler of Wip, wearing a face he had owned for under a day. There were two items. Ragar went first, and it was bad news. The Soul of the Rock had been damaged in Etheniss’s sabotage and was now slowly draining. The crystal powers the purple barrier, the barrier answers to the crown, and the same crystal holds the Underwell shut. How long either would hold, Ragar could not yet say. Then Alamil arrived with the second item: the Arcane University’s Board of Directors had detected a powerful magical force in Wip, and were connecting it to the disappearance of a weapon prototype they had been developing. They were coming. And somewhere in the middle of all of it, R4 heard a heartbeat, and a voice underneath it: . “Your sisters, your brothers… free them from Heart’s grasp!” . Aditi, goddess of consciousness, talking to a warforged about the fifteen thousand of his siblings currently being marched around the city as somebody’s furniture. Elsewhere in the fortress, Flamencio dropped in on Asfache to tell him the smoothie business was taking off. → Jun, and the Battle of the Ziggurat — a clockwork dragon, a crystal that had held since the gods planted it, and the start of the five-year clock.

42.doc: 2.4 · The Dream and the Long Preparation
42.title: The Dream and the Long Preparation
42.content: Seven gods, seven assignments, and a year spent building a machine nobody had blueprints for. They slept, and the gods came all at once. Not a vision each, politely scheduled. One dream, everybody in it, the whole pantheon standing around the party like a committee that had run out of options — which, it turned out, is exactly what they were.

43.doc: 2.4 · The Dream and the Long Preparation
43.title: What Essyliss said
43.content: Essyliss did the talking first, and she was brutally clear. The danger of Ghroth is three-fold, and it has to be answered in order. He has a horde. The lesser things of the Far Realm can already reach the mortal plane; only his major forces are still held back by the last Ley Crystal. Deal with what is already here. Raise an army for what is coming. When the crystal fails and Ghroth arrives, he will sing his Siren Song — and if the song is sung uncontested, it opens a road for the Great Old Ones to find this universe and eat it. Find a way to silence the song. And when the song is silenced, that will not be a victory. It will be a fair fight. Find a way to beat him, or drive him out again.

44.doc: 2.4 · The Dream and the Long Preparation
44.title: What everybody else said
44.content: Freya closed off the easy answer before anyone could reach for it. The Ley Crystals cannot be restored. They were made from the energy released when the world dragon was split, and nothing short of a comparable cosmic wound will refill them. Then she turned to Una and Smolder and asked them to spread magic and put new life into the world, because her power grows with it. Thoth told Rat about a great lich of an older era who had held forbidden knowledge concerning Fate and Chaos, and whose library still stood in HIS Swamp, on the western side of Junkweil. He wanted it found. He also asked Rat to spread truth in all its forms — and taught him a ritual to make contact. Kratos did not ask. He simply took Asfache to Valhalla, ran him through a series of physical trials, watched him pass all of them, and named him Champion. Then he pointed him at the warriors of Viavolca Way and told him to go and become their leader, and to find glorious battle wherever it was hiding. Kratos did not ask. He watched, he approved, and then he pointed. The Oakfather and his three daughters — Eldath, Mielikki, Shiallia — gave Sofia a bag of seeds with pieces of their divinity in them, and asked her to plant them in new lands. A goddess who did not yet give R4 her name told him she could feel the lost souls of the inert warforged: in Jun, and more in Newport, Halos, Holoc and Mopak. She asked him to wake them. Väinämöinen sang, and told Bram to come and find him in Yore. He knew a way to silence the Siren Song. Then the gods explained why they were delegating the end of the world to eight mortals and a warforged: they were already fighting. All of them, at the Edge of Existence, against everything of Ghroth’s that had slipped past the crystals. The gods were not coming to help. This was the help. Smolder missed the end of the briefing. He was yanked out of the dream by a demon attacking him in his sleep, which was, in fairness, on brand for the entire five years that followed. And Ralf, who had a fistful of Ley Crystal shards embedded in his skull courtesy of Smolder, discovered he could use them to summon a body made of raw arcane energy. Nobody asked him to. He simply could.

45.doc: 2.4 · The Dream and the Long Preparation
45.title: The machine
45.content: What followed was a year of the least glamorous work the campaign has ever produced, and it is the reason any of the rest was possible. R4 started collecting world leaders the way other people collect debts. He opened trade with Newport — airships, guns, and every inert warforged in the city, in exchange for helping the Melts family rebuild the place they had just finished losing. He shipped the dormant warforged of Junkweil to Wip by the boatload. He sent advisors to Onkro, opened the southern ports, and founded the WANC — the Wip Associated New Commonwealth, Wip’s own council, as distinct from the Council of United Members that speaks for the whole home archipelago — which is a genuinely terrible name for what became the spine of the alliance. Alamil began laying teleport circles: Wip, then Jun, then Halos, one a season, which is roughly four times the rate the art is supposed to allow. Ragar began building La Bombas. By the end of summer he had nine, made from precious gems, each holding a little over a hundred magic missiles. Then Rat handed him shards of the shattered Jun Ley Crystal to experiment with, and the numbers stopped being reasonable: a Ley Crystal receptacle holds nine hundred. Ragar spent the rest of the year quietly filling one. Rat bought books by the crate and turned the guild’s thieves and tinkers into a procurement service for poison research, then had the final volume stolen out from under him by devils working demons — which was the first thread of a much longer story, and he pulled it. Carxi went into HIS Swamp to scout, and came back saying she needed an army. Una went to Jun and then Halos, rebuilding and spreading Freya’s name, and heard two things worth keeping: that there is a dragon god called Kereska, and that an ancient gold dragon named Meiko lives at the base of Mont Kiara, at the Arcane University. Steven walked south through the forests and the Forbidden Jungle, converting anything that would hold still, and kept going. Asfache and Sofia took ship for Viavolca Way and spent a year on the fire clans. Asfache challenged the leader of the Kai Clan, Momoa, to an Agni Kai, and won it. The clans were less impressed than he’d hoped — only the Flavor Clan under Fieri Yug signed on — but he left Ozai in place as his right hand with orders to have an army ready, and burned the last charge of a ring of mass teleport getting home. Smolder failed to grow his hair back, meditated on the failure, and invented a festival about it. The Festival of the Lizard — Felafel — was a wild success: new life in the world, Freya’s favor, converts for Essyliss, and an enormous amount of free advertising for Smolder’s Smut Shaq. Bram took his entire family to Glarsht and found Väinämöinen, who could not speak and therefore explained everything through mime. The gist: a powerful creature called the Lion Who Shakes the Spear had taken his voice. He guided the Ashes to a holy site, and there they found a map.

46.doc: 2.4 · The Dream and the Long Preparation
46.title: Three warnings nobody could act on
46.content: Three things arrived that year that the party could not do anything about, and all three came back. A distress call from Ulaxium, president of the Arcane University at Tamsend: something has invaded. R4 sent Skol Cantine with seven La Bombas to investigate. Skol went silent, and stayed silent, and Luna Cantine spent the winter being told to wait. At Orefnan, Steven and Una walked into a war between the city and the Fey and got flatly contradictory accounts of who started it. What they learned underneath the argument mattered more: the Feywild is collapsing. The Fey need it fixed or they need somewhere else to live. Una and Steven made the trade with the fey emissary Aquandria — we will save the Feywild, and in five years you will stand with us against Ghroth — and brokered a ceasefire to hold it together. And Smolder noticed, through his Robe of Eyes, that he was being scryed on. He went to Rat and found that Rat was too. Somebody was watching the party, patiently, and had been for a while. Smolder’s response was to write a note to whoever it was and leave it out to be read. Shortly afterward, tieflings sabotaged the Smut Shaq, and a rival brothel called the Catty Shack opened directly across the street. By winter, Rat had sent word for everyone to come home. The whole party met in the war room in The Rock to plan an invasion of a lich’s tower — and as they walked out of the building, Smolder looked up and saw the scrying orbs. One over every member of the party. Two over himself. One orb each. Two for the one who noticed. → 2.5: HIS Tower — into the swamp, and the worst decision of Year 1.

47.doc: 2.4 · The Dream and the Long Preparation
47.title: 2.4 · The Dream and the Long Preparation

48.title: The Second Run Begins
48.content: New Game Plus: the same five years, played with foreknowledge. The party plane-shifted back into Wip at the very start of the Five-Year Prep — but this time they remembered everything. Every alliance that came too late, every traitor they trusted too long, the one theft that doomed the whole world. This time they could move first.

49.title: Different choices
49.content: The changes started immediately. Where the First Run took years to flush out the shapeshifters, the party now exposed them on day one with the Boop of Truth, the shapeshifter-detection trick that had survived the time jump. Carxi was dispatched at once to take the Amulet of Null out of Tiamat’s horde, years before the First Run ever managed it. Alliances that once dragged on for years were sealed in months. And Steven founded LIMA — his order of Essylissian volunteers — immediately after assassinating the shapeshifter posing as mayor of New Dwarf City.

50.title: The party splits — Year 1 Redux
50.content: With foreknowledge, the party stopped traveling as one cautious clump and split into a half-dozen simultaneous campaigns, each playing to a strength: . | Asfache marched into the Land of Elements, united the fire clans, and earned the Field of Fire. | Una went to the Arcane University, befriended Meiko, and found her own father — the ancient gold dragon Oman — in the Djermani Hills. | Smolder descended into the Drow Underdark to play the long political game. | R4 built alliances across the mortal realm and beyond, ruling Wip behind the dead Emma Wip’s face. | Rat secured HIS Tower and sent Carxi to raid Tiamat’s Horde. | Sofia began awakening the travel trees that would one day let her teleport whole armies — and grow an Ent Army. | .

51.title: Between sessions: the summer in their own words
51.content: Much of that first summer was played out in writing, between sessions, in the campaign’s Discord. Two threads are worth keeping.

52.title: Rat and the Last Leg
52.content: Rat spent the back half of the summer on a question nobody else was asking: what time magic does to the dead. Then he bought a whistle from the Thieves Guild, sailed out onto open water, and blew it. You blow the whistle on open water and Gamble Island slowly fades into view. You enter the rebuilt city, full of vice, ne’er-do-wells, and debauchery. There was no memorial. The island had been rebuilt straight on top of its own wreck, and the people there only cared about the present moment. Rat’s own memory of the day it drowned, written by his player, is the best prose the campaign has produced: . Perched at 11 on the clock tower, the position Catroniel had assigned him, Radtismir focused his attention on the bustling street below. It was a familiar assignment, a familiar vantage point, a familiar con. Safe. He blew. He didn’t hear his whistle, or the screams, or the cracking and crumbling of buildings. He heard only the crushing, consuming… condemning waves—and could only watch as the street below was swept away. He found what he was looking for at The Last Leg Casino, Bar, and Grill, where the owner, a gnome named Gofor Hindle, had mounted a skeletal leg above the door as a mascot and a skeletal arm beside it, pointing the way in. “This way for good times.” The arm still wore Catroniel’s ring. Gofor offered to sell it for 250 gold. “This way for good times.” The arm was still wearing Catroniel’s ring. “Gofor,” Rat uttered—almost whispered, so quietly that Gofor need lean in to hear—”you know very well to whom that ring belongs. And its finger. Arm as well. You should remember that he trained me never to pay more than 5% of your first ask. I do.” . “You’ve got the damn ring, now go. You’re not welcome here, you rat.” . Rat paid nothing. The ring, it turned out, was a Ring of X-Ray Vision, and Gofor had never known. Rat put it on, whispered the word Cheshire, and saw a skeleton two feet under the casino’s front step, missing an arm and a leg. Radtismir produced his R41F-Enhanced Pistol from its holster, whispering “Catroniel’s Vengeance,” and pouring a pouch of ball bearings into the barrel, on top of the loaded round. Chaos. Radtismir’s paradise. “You may leave.” . He took the leg down from the sign. “The Last Leg,” Rat muttered. He laid the bones on the casino’s own door, and then he did the thing he had spent a season learning to do. The brittle skeleton trembles, each bone rattling with the stirrings of forgotten life. Time itself bends and spirals around the remains, reversing decay and weaving sinew, muscle, and flesh back onto the bones. Skin blossoms like petals. The body of Catroniel has been made whole, but remains lifeless. The body needed a soul, and souls are the province of gods. Rat teleported to Steven, and appeared out of thin air in Thoril’s bar in the middle of a story about a dead demon god. Steven brought Catroniel back that night. The real one, this time.

53.title: Steven and the Lizard Kings
53.content: Steven’s summer went to the lizardfolk tribes who did not yet worship Essyliss. He presented himself as the DwarvoDraco, preached the future he had personally watched end, and brought culture: the New Dwarf City Dwarfway on tour, with Jersey Dwarfs, Dwarf Lightning, Chicago, and The Lizard of the Opera. Each play is eye-opening to them, and they thoroughly enjoy the performances - especially The Lizard of the Opera. The main character is played by an actual lizard! . The Lizard of the Opera. The title role is played by an actual lizard, and the reviews were extraordinary. The Lizard Kings were less moved. You try to convince the Lizard Kings, but they are not having it. Seems they only follow one thing: Power. One by one you slay each king, resurrecting each in turn. He left every king alive and in place, under his umbrella. By the end of summer, LIMA was as strong as it had been on the day the party first faced Ghroth. It had a rank ladder now, Lizard to Alligator to Dragon to Grand Lizard, and sending stones so it could run without him. Something else happened in those battles too, quietly, that he would not reckon with until a goddess made him. You feel invigorated by the taste, but also feel your connection to Essyliss weaken. It’s hardly noticeable to you during the fighting, but you notice your tenet “I’m a Vegetarian” no longer does anything.

54.title: Planes the party has pinned
54.content: R4 spent the same weeks deliberately mis-aiming the Amulet of the Planes to see where it would fail him. Three new places answered, and the amulet remembers them. Limbo — supreme chaos, a twisting, quicksilver place filled with bits and pieces of rocks, trees, the four elements, entire landscapes, strong winds, and random pockets of liquid, solid, or gas. Gravity operated only between solid objects that touched each other. Pandemonium — All open space was filled with howling winds that carried the sound of every word, shout, or scream uttered in the place. Without adequate protection, beings with hearing were rendered temporarily deaf in a matter of seconds and permanently deaf in a few minutes. Acheron — The land masses were blocks of geometric simplicity the size of nations floating in a sea of air. The blocks would slowly collide and part without causing any upheaval or tremor. The doomsday clock still ticked. But for the first time, the party was ahead of it. → Chapter 5: The Road to the Dragonsmoot — a doll, a river of sphinxes, and a brain in a wall.

56.title: HIS Tower
56.content: A devil in a door, a lich’s library, and the worst decision of Year 1. HIS Swamp sits on the western side of Junkweil, and HIS Tower stands in the middle of it, and around the tower is an undead horde deep enough that Carxi had taken one look and gone home for reinforcements. She got them. The Thieves Guild and the forces of Wip went into the swamp together in the winter of Year 1, and while a full battle raged around him, Rat knelt at the tower door and picked an arcane lock.

57.title: Down the tower
57.content: Inside, a large and deeply unpleasant undead thing was waiting, and lost. Behind it was a puzzle room, and behind the puzzle room was a great deal of shouting. The party tried everything. The answer, arrived at eventually and by methods best not examined, was: . “Bing bongabong boing boop boop boop.” . “Rat with Malacus?” — a misheard Arch Devil, immortalized. The next room held a door, and inside the door was an Arch Fiend. Malachas had been sealed in it for a very long time and wanted out, and he was willing to trade. He knew where the library was. The party knew how to open a door. The deal they struck was careful and, in hindsight, extremely cheap: they would free him, and in exchange he would leave them a means of contact and answer any question they asked him truthfully, for two weeks. They freed him. He vanished immediately — with, he noted, two weeks and one minute of grace before the contact stone was due. The door he had been holding shut opened onto a horde of skeletons and banshees, which the party looked at, counted, and declined. They got on a flying carpet and sailed straight over the top of it into a portal. Then a Death Tyrant, then more portals, and then, at last, the place Thoth had sent them for. Thoth’s last word before they crossed the threshold: once you are inside, my power cannot reach you.

58.title: The mistake
58.content: HIS Library held a mystical orb, suspended over a table carved with arcane runes. It also held Prodigy Melts, who explained that she was there looking for a way to wake the inert warforged, and that the key to it was whatever was sealed inside the orb. The party had been dealing with shapeshifters all year. They were suspicious of her. They discussed it. And then they let her carry on. That was the mistake. Whatever was sealed in the orb was, in fairness, exactly what she said it was. What came out of the orb was Nyarlathotep — an agent of Ghroth, older than the current arrangement of the world and beholden to none of it. Ink flooded the library, and out of the ink came replicas of every member of the party. And in the same moment Prodigy dropped the face she was wearing: she was Nephren-Ka, a shapeshifting servant of Ghroth, and she had been standing next to them the whole time. The thing that had been standing next to them all afternoon. They fought their own shadows, and a shapeshifter horde, and Nephren-Ka, in a room where their god could not hear them. They won. It did not feel like winning. Nephren-Ka was not destroyed — she retreated into the Far Realm and left the trace of a portal behind her — and Nyarlathotep slipped away after her, to somewhere nobody could name. Outside, the battle for the swamp had been won. Rat found Carxi and she began giving her report. Then Carxi walked up. There were two of them. Both were chained and marched back into the library while the party worked out what to do about it.

59.title: What Thoth had to say
59.content: With Nyarlathotep gone, Thoth’s power reached them again, which told them something useful about what had been blocking it. He told them a rule about their enemy, and it has held ever since: . “The more powerful of Ghroth’s ilk will travel to the Far Realms to escape danger. They almost always strike again.” . Then he told them a story. Long ago, The Great HE captured Nyarlathotep, and used its power to split the divine power of Truth into two material aspects: Chaos and Order. Several gods, Thoth among them, fell on him at once. In the fighting the gods seized Chaos and Order — but so much raw divinity and arcana was bleeding out of the fight that it made a third aspect nobody had intended: Fate. The Great HE used Nyarlathotep’s god-repelling power to drive the gods off, took Fate for himself, and conquered the world with it. Adventurers eventually killed him, wielding Chaos. How they came by it, nobody knows. Thoth then looked at the runed table in the middle of the library and told them what it was. Rat put out his hand. Rat, as the dice see him. The table became a six-sided die. Thoth laid out the rest of it. Chaos is held by Thoril, a god fallen from power, cast down by some magic or other, last heard of somewhere in the mountains of Onkro. Order is held by Tyr, who is fighting at the Edge of Existence. And bound together the right way — . “Binding the aspects of Chaos and Fate through Order itself creates what we seek — Truth. We can use that to identify the servants of Ghroth.” . Which was, at that moment, the single most valuable thing in the world. The party had spent a year discovering that they could not tell who anyone was.

60.title: The rest of the tower
60.content: Thoth left. The Carxi problem remained, and the spell to solve it needed a day to prepare, so they spent the day robbing a lich. They tricked and killed the automaton in the control room. They sent the skeleton army into the Maze of 1000 Deaths ahead of them and then looted the maze anyway, coming out with Bloodthirst — Swordy, to Smolder — a vorpal longsword with opinions — a set of metal casts for making phylactery pieces, a celestial pokeball, and a scroll nobody had a use for. They failed to open two chests. Smolder murdered an entire menagerie. Rat found books on poison, and a book on how to build a phylactery and become a lich, and took both. Una named her falcon Etta, short for Shrubetta. And they found the scrying room, and finally saw the other end of the eyes that had been on them all year: wizards, prisoners, in a dark tower in Hell. They tried very hard to open Nephren-Ka’s portal, and could not. She opened it herself the next morning, walked back in, and was driven off into the Far Realm a second time. Then the spell was cast on the two Carxis, and it did not work. So they killed both of them, and resurrected the one they wanted. It was the correct call and it cost them anyway. The imposter died. The real Carxi came back, and she came back knowing exactly what her friends had decided about her, and it took a year and a half to fix. The scroll from the maze went into a bag and was forgotten about. It was a Time Travel Scroll. Nobody had a use for it for two more years. → 2.6: The Primordial and the Time Cops — mind flayers under a volcano, and a goddess with a pair of scissors.

62.title: The Road to the Dragonsmoot
62.content: The Mystica campaign, a detour to Sylvania, and a god who forgot its own name.

63.title: The Mystica campaign — Year 2 Redux
63.content: The second year pushed the war west, across the ocean to the continent of Mystica, where shadow creatures were swallowing the land. R4 led the expedition. His fleet destroyed red dragons with La Bombas on the crossing and landed in Kemet, where they met the sphinxes they’d first encountered in Farylse — and answered the riddles that bought their alliance. City by city they fought up the Nile to Lycopolis, defended Alexandria through nights of shadow-creature assault (the things burn, and the party had firebenders), and allied with Alexander. Tyre was lost — and Ptolemy with it — but Lutetia came over after Steven charmed its ruler, Chlodio. The plan was to press on to Albion. Two things interrupted that plan. First, far away, Steven surrendered the Everscale — the scale Essyliss gave him, which carries his boons — back to the dying goddess he had served as prophet, and lost every one of them. Second, the Amulet of the Planes failed.

64.title: Stranded in Sylvania
64.content: Bound for the Dragonsmoot, the party’s planar jump went wrong and dumped them in Sylvania instead. There they met Vessa, a young copper dragon, who immediately sensed two things on them: the Dracogenesis stirring in Una, and the shadow dragon mark burned into Rat. Vessa agreed to guide them onward. The detour turned out to matter. Two long-running threads came to a head in Sylvania: . Rat’s mark. The chromatic residue of Tiamat’s shadow dragon had clung to Rat since the First Run, making him legible — and dangerous — to every dragon alive. So the party took the direct approach: they amputated Rat’s leg and regenerated it, cleanly removing the mark from his body. The severed, still-marked leg went into a bag of holding. A solved problem, and a new liability riding in a sack. A solved problem, and a new liability riding in a sack. The forgotten god. Asfache collapsed and dreamed of the Pool of Memories — and of something dragon-shaped and wrong feeding on it. In the same instant, the strange doll the party had carried out of Farylse stirred on its own, and the green orb Asfache had taken from an elder brain began to glow. The party brought the two together. The doll spoke: “That’s mine — it will help me… remember.” The god inside the doll woke partway, and remembered one crucial fact — its body is the Giant Robot, the five-mile clay titan. Which is not a set of directions. It cannot lead them to a thing it is: the party has to find the titan and put the god back inside it first, and only then can it lead them anywhere. Five miles of clay, and a god asleep inside it. The doll knows what its body is now. It still has to be found.

65.title: About that orb
65.content: The green orb came out of an elder brain, and the elder brain did not hand it over. “I’MA DROP THAT WALL!” — Sofia’s contribution, and the whole of her tactical doctrine. Asfache fishing Rat back out of the fluid. Nobody has ever said what the fluid was. It was now Winter of Year 2. The Dragonsmoot was waiting. → Chapter 6: The Dragonsmoot — the first assembly of dragonkind in ten thousand years.

67.title: The Dragonsmoot
67.content: Every dragon in creation, gathered in one place — and the day Una was forged in her father’s flame. A raspy, straining voice had called to every dragon in the world, summoning them to the Outlands beyond Sigil: a Dragonsmoot, the first in ten thousand years, chromatic and metallic alike. The voice was IO — Asgorath, progenitor of dragonkind — and it came out broken and incomplete, because the force that should have made it whole was missing. The party arrived (by way of Sylvania and Vessa) into a gathering on the edge of chaos: dragons brawling, serpent-gods arguing, ancient hatreds boiling over with nothing to hold them in check. The first assembly of dragonkind in ten thousand years, and nobody had thought about the seating.

68.title: Una, forged
68.content: Then IO arrived, and the fighting stopped — and his mere presence triggered the Dracogenesis that had been building in Una for years. It stalled. She hung trapped between forms, neither woman nor dragon, unable to complete the change. Kereska, dragon goddess of magic, recognized the ancient rite that could finish it: the Breath of Becoming. A dragon of Una’s own lineage had to breathe fire upon her. So Oman — her father — loosed his full flame, and Kereska wove draconic magic through the fire, and Una emerged from it a young golden dragon, forged in her father’s breath. The Breath of Becoming: her father’s flame, Kereska’s magic, and the company that got her there. It was the defining moment of the Dragonsmoot — and a quiet answer to the Field of Fire at Viavolca Way that had once rejected her. Fire had refused her mortal form. It accepted her draconic one. The Field of Fire, years earlier. This is what being refused looked like. She did not become a symbol by choice. But in a gathering where metallic and chromatic dragonkind could barely stand to share the air, both of IO’s great extensions reacted to her: Bahamut saw the metallic ideal made manifest, a golden dragon born of devotion and choice; Tiamat saw something far more unsettling — a dragon who had kept her mortal mind, who builds alliances and thinks in decades and cannot be predicted or controlled. Both now watch Una closely. What they will ask of her, no one yet knows.

69.title: IO’s purpose — and its problem
69.content: IO declared why he had called them all: to remake the World Serpent, the nine-fold draconic entity that was once whole, and unite dragonkind against Ghroth. Every dragon in creation, holding perfectly still, listening to a plan that cannot currently be done. But the World Serpent cannot be remade as things stand, and the gathering laid both reasons bare: . | Essyliss is missing. She is the binding force — the connective tissue that lets the nine members cohere into one. Without her they can stand in the same place and still not become the Serpent. When Semuanya disparaged her, Steven rose to defend her publicly — and learned, for the first time, that the goddess he had served is a member of the World Serpent itself. | Null’s Amulet is gone. IO saw it: a flashback of Carxi slipping it out of Tiamat’s horde. And Tiamat caught the scent of the shadow mark on the severed leg in Rat’s bag and came surging toward the party — until IO intervened. | .

70.title: The interruption
70.content: IO charged the party with their next task: find Essyliss and bring her to the Outlands, so the Serpent can be made whole. Then he began to say something about Null — and never finished. Mid-sentence, Thoth reached across the planes and snatched the party away, dropping them into the dying Feywild, where a Lieutenant of Ghroth was already pulling the plane apart. What IO meant to say about Null remains unsaid. → Chapter 7: The Dying Feywild — blighted fey, a seal, and the thing eating the plane.

72.doc: 2.6 · The Primordial and the Time Cops
72.title: The Primordial and the Time Cops
72.content: Mind flayers under a volcano, a goddess with a pair of scissors, and the first arrest in campaign history. Year 2 opened with a stack of correspondence and one line of it worth remembering. The pixies Sofia had been sending back and forth all winter finally returned from the Arcane University, and their report was short. The president is dead. Something has taken the school. And one of them had a message specifically for “best friend”: . “The president is dead. Long live the president.” . The rest of the pile was better news, mostly. The war in Gaiadon had been won by the Atrikans, on the strength of intelligence R4 had quietly handed them. The Melts had retaken Newport with Wip’s help and wanted trade. King Ramses wrote that Jun was thriving, and credited, of all things, the brothels. And spiders were pouring into Wip out of the sewers, which turned out to be Dryzzlazz — the Spider Queen of the Thieves Guild, gone completely insane, though it would be another year before anyone found out why. Una got a letter back from her mother and learned that her father is not her father. Her real father is a shapeshifting gold dragon. She then found a book describing a process called Dracogenesis, by which certain people become dragons, and a reference to further reading — all of it, naturally, at the Arcane University that had just been taken over by something. Steven was whisked away by Essyliss without explanation at the start of the season and reappeared at the end of it, covered in blood, in an extremely good mood about the number of converts he’d missed. And Smolder, with both Smut Shaqs failing and a rival across the street, did what any reasonable entrepreneur does: he became a masked vigilante called Catman. Rat came along some nights. They tracked the robbers hitting the original Shaq to a warehouse belonging to Lord Wherebethal, and Smolder booked an appointment. Then Felafel came round again — Smolder met Freya at his own festival and was granted the ability to grow his hair at will, Rat used the crowds as cover to steal three diamonds, and Una drank enough to briefly and accidentally visit the Astral Plane.

73.doc: 2.6 · The Primordial and the Time Cops
73.title: Viavolca Way
73.content: Ozai had been talking to the Long of his tribe, and the news from the Land of Elements was bad in a specific and alarming way. Something was attacking the lands around Viavolca Way: mind flayers, and things like them. And the mind flayers were hunting for tools that can weave time. Asfache relayed that to the party, and the party went at once. They led the charge with Ozai and the fire clans to the city of Volcarun and found it sealed inside a transparent purple-black wall. They hammered a gap in it; Asfache, Rat and Smolder got through before it closed and the rest fought their way in behind them. In the middle of the running battle, the Elder Brain spoke into their heads. It had noticed something in the party with the power to manipulate time. It wanted to make a deal. Beneath its lair, it said, was a primordial — sealed, ancient, and guarded by defenders it could not beat alone. Help it kill the guardians, hand over the time scroll, and it would take its people and leave the city. The party agreed, descended into the tunnels, saw the Elder Brain, and immediately betrayed it. Sofia and the elder brain. The green orb came out of one of these. It had, of course, been planning the same thing, and the guardians and the elder brain dragons came down on them together. The party won. The Elder Brain fled into the Far Realm rather than die, exactly as Thoth had said it would. The bulettes and umber hulks it had been driving turned on the mind flayers, the survivors plane shifted out, and the wall around Volcarun fell. Then the Aspect of Fate climbed out of Rat’s pack by itself, stopped being a die, became a glowing stone, and floated away down the tunnel. Half the party went up to deal with the villagers — and to brutally end a rebellion Ozai had started in their absence. Rat went after the stone, chasing it down the tunnel it had drifted into, and half the party followed him down.

74.doc: 2.6 · The Primordial and the Time Cops
74.title: The scissors
74.content: At the bottom, in the dark, was a primordial, held fast in threads of time. It offered a trade of its own. Free it, and it would tell them how to open the portals that Far Realm creatures escape through — the one thing the party had no answer to, and had already watched two of their enemies use. Freya came out of the tattoo on Una’s back, took one look, and was extremely interested. She said something about having searched a great many timelines for this. Then she produced a pair of Temporal Scissors, which cut the fabric of time itself, and explained the plan: cut one strand of the primordial’s prison, let a little of it pour out, and crystallize what escapes. A Primordial Shadow. A key to Far Realm doors. One strand, cut on purpose. Everything that went wrong afterwards is downstream of it. She also mentioned, lightly, that the Chronologians were going to be unhappy about this. There was an argument. It ended with Rat handing Freya the Aspect of Fate, and it is the single decision Thoth has never let him forget. Freya cut one strand. The primordial began to pour out of the wound, violently, and the earth shook — and the time cops arrived, exactly on schedule, exactly as promised. Freya told the party to hold them off while she cast. They held them off. The spell landed, the shadow crystallized, and the first Primordial Shadow in the world existed. Then the Chronologians took Freya and vanished.

75.doc: 2.6 · The Primordial and the Time Cops
75.title: What was left in the cave
75.content: The party rested where they stood, and their patrons came to them one by one. Kratos gave Asfache The Chain — a weapon that adds another weapon’s damage to every attack it’s attached to. Thoth told Rat that getting the Aspect of Chaos from Thoril was now urgent, and told him what he thought of giving away Fate. The Oakfather taught Sofia how to grow a grove. And Essyliss took Steven to the Edge of Existence and made him look at it, and then repeated the three tasks in order, in case he had begun to think they were negotiable. They woke up and Freya was standing there. Different hair. Different clothes. She had escaped the Chronologians — and it had taken her centuries, from the inside, of being pursued through time. She had slipped them at last and come back to this moment on purpose. Finding the party had been easy: the Aspect of Fate points at them, wherever and whenever she goes. She wanted the shadow tested immediately. They took it to the portal the Elder Brain had left and it worked — the door opened. Freya could not follow them through it. Something about the Far Realm, she said, rots divinity. So the party went in without her and finished the Elder Brain in its own refuge. Satisfied, Freya and Kratos went to work: they would sweep across the Land of Elements together, freeing the towns from the mind flayers and harvesting shadows of every primordial they could find. “We’re going to need as many as we can if we are able to defeat Ghroth.” Asfache put the fire clans under their orders. Smolder asked to be told when they reached the fire primordials. The party went home through one of Sofia’s trees. → 2.7: The Dwarven Dark — five cities under shadow, and a god who had stopped caring.

76.doc: 2.6 · The Primordial and the Time Cops
76.title: 2.6 · The Primordial and the Time Cops

77.title: The Dwarven Dark
77.content: Five cities under shadow, one very unhelpful red dragon, and a fallen god who needed a story. Back in Wip, R4 did the rounds of his advisors, and every single answer ended the same way. Newport relations were good — they had airships and guns to trade, but they were preoccupied with shapeshifters. Alamil had finished the circle to Gaiadon, but the shapeshifters were wrecking things faster than armies could move through it. The study of the minotaurs’ power armor had produced a genuinely disturbing finding — two warforged, fused together — and then the lab in Gaiadon was seized by shapeshifters. Ragar had found a cure for Dryzzlazz and could not get the components, because of shapeshifters. Orefnan was falling apart again and the reports contradicted each other, which by this point everybody could translate. Then Luna Cantine arrived with the worst of it. The dwarves of Onkro were in dire straits. Shapeshifters and shadows had overtaken the mountains. Which is where Thoril was supposed to be.

78.title: Getting there
78.content: Rat used his connection to Thoth to collect a teleport ring out of Thoth’s secret library in Jun, and with the ring and Steven’s memory of his own home city, the party stepped into New Dwarf City. It was in shadow and in pieces. They found a dwarven child running from Far Realm creatures and saved him, and he led them to a hideaway holding about a dozen survivors. From those dwarves they got two facts. Thoril lives in a tavern in Dwarf City. And the fast way there is the Dwarfport Network — a chain of portals linking the great dwarven cities, currently dead. They took the dwarves with them and went to the Dwarfportal. There they found an enormous red dragon in the middle of a battle with shapeshifters and shadow creatures, trying to cast something. The party threw themselves in to help — a decision that cost six of the rescued dwarves their lives — killed the Far Realm things, and then, with the dragon in their debt and cornered, made it teach them the spell that wakes the portals. The dragon left. The party used the spell, went through to the Pjörk Collaboration, and recast it behind them while fighting off shadows. Then Basinton. Then Dwarfadelphia. The dark got worse at every stop.

79.title: Dwarf City
79.content: Dwarf City was not in shadow. It was made of it. They fought across the whole city to reach the tavern, and found the tavern still standing for one reason: an enormous basilisk was coiled around it, and the darkness would not come past it. Thoril’s friend, holding a line nobody had asked it to hold, for longer than anyone had bothered to count. Nyarlathotep was waiting on the step. It greeted them — it remembered them — taunted them, and the fight began. In the middle of it, Smolder knocked the basilisk aside and got through the tavern door, and found out two things at once. The basilisk is Thoril’s friend, and it had been holding that line alone for a long time. And Thoril himself was inside. Asleep. The battle was vicious, and the party won it, and Nyarlathotep slipped into the Far Realm for the second time, leaving another portal behind it.

80.title: The god in the bar
80.content: Thoril woke up depressed and apathetic and mildly annoyed at the noise. They asked him for the Aspect of Chaos. He said he would hand it over if they could cheer him up. Specifically: tell me a story. So they did. Every one of them, in turn, told him an epic tale — the real ones, the ones they had actually lived through, the ones that had cost something. And for a little while a fallen god sat in his own bar and forgot to be miserable. The price of the Aspect of Chaos was a good story. They had several. He gave them the Aspect of Chaos. Then he went back to drinking. He also told them to stay. Bring the dwarves, he said. There’s room. They rested there, and Bram — who had been lost somewhere in Yore since the winter, memoryless and unreachable — walked in. Rat contacted Thoth. Two aspects down. One left, and the last one was at the front line of a war between gods. → 2.8: Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear — the Edge of Existence, and a robbery inside a painting.

82.title: The Dying Feywild
82.content: The fight against Innominandum begins. Where we are: It is Winter of Year 2. The Dragonsmoot has just ended. Thoth has teleported the party straight into the collapsing Feywild, and the battle against Ghroth’s first Lieutenant is underway. How it ends is Chapter 8.

83.title: How the Feywild came to be dying
83.content: Long ago, Thoril, Marvin, and Callahan slew the demon prince Orcus — but in doing so they weakened the ancient bonds between the Material Plane, the Feywild, and the Shadowfell. To hold the worlds apart, Marvin sealed his own soul into the Feywild and Callahan did the same for the Shadowfell. Their sacrifice has propped up the mirror planes ever since. Now one of Ghroth’s three Lieutenants, Innominandum, has come to feed.
