It is draining the Feywild’s essence through Marvin’s Seal, growing stronger with every passing moment — and as the Feywild fails, so does one of the walls protecting the mortal world.

84.title: The fight in progress
84.content: Thoth dropped the party out of the Dragonsmoot and directly into it. Innominandum looms as a massive, gnarled tree-entity, draining the seal through six great roots. High above the canopy, Freya, Kratos, and Thoril battle the thing directly — but they cannot kill it while it feeds. Cutting it off from the seal is the party’s job. They came out swinging. In the first round they severed five of the six roots. But Innominandum’s hunger has consequences: blighted fey — once-beautiful dryads and treants, now corrupted into something wrong — are clawing their way toward the seal. Inside the golden dome of light, Marvin’s spirit flickers — tired, fading, but still holding. Five roots down in the first round. The sixth is the one the whole plane hangs on. One root remains. A week ago these were the most beautiful things in creation.

85.title: What comes next
85.content: The plan from here is clear, even if surviving it isn’t: . | Sever the last root and drive Innominandum off the seal. | Pursue it into the Far Realm using the Primordial Shadow fragments — the only way to stop a Far Realm entity from simply fleeing through a portal and regenerating — and destroy it for good. | Reseal the Feywild. Thoril will commune with his old friend Marvin and pour half of his own life force into a new seal, freeing Marvin’s trapped soul. | . And then there is the other half of the work, still waiting in the dark: the Shadowfell, where Tenebrosum feeds on Callahan’s seal exactly as Innominandum feeds here. But that is the next chapter. For now, there is one root left, a god flickering inside a dome of light, and a tree the size of the sky that must not be allowed to finish its meal. → Chapter 8: Seventy-One Hours — how it ended, and what it cost.

87.title: Seventy-One Hours
87.content: The first Lieutenant dies. Everything it cost, and the clock that started the moment it fell. Where we are: Innominandum is dead — the first of Ghroth’s three Lieutenants ever to fall. The Feywild is whole. The party is back in Wip with a long rest, twelve hours of quiet, and a countdown they cannot pause.

88.title: The last root
88.content: They cut it — and Innominandum came down out of the canopy onto Marvin’s seal directly, and raised a titan out of the beauty it had stolen: one last thing standing between the party and the door it was eating. It was driven off anyway. And then it ran, the way its kind always runs: through a hole in the world, into the Far Realm, where nothing that could kill it was supposed to be able to follow. The party followed it.

89.title: What they gave up at the threshold
89.content: Divine things do not cross. So at the edge of the portal the party set them down in a pile on the grass: . | Una put down her entire dragonhood — Kereska’s consecration, Freya’s aspect, Etta the falcon — eleven hours after she had been forged into it, and walked into hell as something less. | Asfache left the green orb, and watched Cal dissolve in front of him for the second time in his life, knowingly, and went in anyway. | Rat lost Thoth entirely. The man who built a life out of hearing what other people can’t, walking into a place where everything was talking and none of it was language. | R4 lost Aditi, and with her the ability to touch another mind — alone inside his own head for the first time since the day he woke up. | Steven had already lost his goddess. What the Far Realm gave him instead was that his Siren Song teeth got stronger there. The one part of him Essyliss punished is the part that place feeds. | Smolder went bald. | . Everything divine, left on the grass. They walked in as themselves and nothing else. Six of them crossed: Rat, R4, Steven, Smolder, Una, Asfache.

90.title: The Wrong Garden
90.content: On the other side was a garden built out of everything Innominandum had eaten — beautiful, wrong, and running on machinery that had no business existing in a place like that. Sofia was inside it. Beautiful, and running on gears. She was hanging in the middle of it with her eyes open. She had gone into Innominandum as an air elemental and could not get out, and it had found a use for her. The frog sac Ghroth’s Siren Song put in her throat during the First Run turned out to be a receiver. Innominandum hollowed her out and put its network in the empty space, and used her to talk to the other two. Una and Rat flew in and pulled her out. She came out breathing. What it cost her, before they reached her, bought most of what the party now knows: where Tenebrosum is and how it feeds, what Mappo No Ryujin looks like, how much of the Pool of Memories is left — and the one genuine gift in all of it, that Mappo is anchored to the Pool and cannot leave it. Whenever the party goes, it will be waiting exactly there. They choose the moment. She has not woken since, and she will not.

91.title: The governorless engine
91.content: Six hands on the tendrils — every one of them chose to stay. Losing, Innominandum reached into its own engine and tore out the governor — choosing to detonate the realm rather than be killed in it. Asfache saw the tendrils still trailing off the torn-out controls and called everyone onto them. R4 had the Amulet of the Planes in his hand and an exit for all of them, and did not use it. And the whole party took hold at once and became the governor themselves — six pairs of hands forcing a limit onto a machine that had none. The engine slowed. Innominandum, with nothing left to root in and nowhere to hide, materialized inside its own works. Smolder and Rat killed it there.

92.title: Seventy years
92.content: Thoth, Kratos, and Freya watch Thoril hold the dome. Marvin’s seal finished the fight at full strength — not cracked, not scarred, not leaking. Whole. That did not happen on its own. During the fight, while everyone else was busy, R4 poured seventy years of his Farylse time into the dome. Seventy years of the time the party carried out of a plane they can never return to, spent quietly into a golden shell so a dead man could keep holding a door. That is why the Feywild recovers whole instead of carrying grey scars forever. That is why Aquandria pledged the entire fey host to the Edge of Existence — every court, unconditionally, the largest alliance win of the Second Run. And that is why Marvin got a last lucid conversation before he settled permanently into the seal. Nobody thanked him. Nobody has done the arithmetic yet.

93.title: What it cost
93.content: Sofia. Her throat is open along its full length and breathes on its own. Her eyes do not close. Her pulse and her breathing run at two different speeds. Sometimes she says things in a language nobody can read, to nobody at all. Nothing fixes this — not the Oakfather, not restoration, not wishes. Mielikki came to the grove, stopped at the edge, said nothing, and wept. Eldath asked permission to come and sit with her once a week. The Oakfather did not come. Horus and Nubia, spent to keep the party standing. Only Bast is left. Half of Thoril, with the other half already owed to Callahan’s door. And where Innominandum was rooted there is a circle of grey ground two hundred feet across where nothing grows. The fey are calling it The Silence, and they will still be calling it that in a thousand years.

94.title: The modron
94.content: Pentad-Nine, riding out of the Far Realm on the one who chooses hardest. Something else walked out of the wreckage. Pentad-Nine was the engine’s limiter — a Mechanus pentadrone that Innominandum tore out of its governor-seat and fed into the gears. It survived. It watched six creatures that are not supposed to be predictable choose to take the governor’s place, with an exit available and declined, and it concluded that this was impossible and had happened anyway. Its verdict: “the proof is incomplete” — the proof being the one Primus accepted from outside Mechanus, that Ghroth’s end is inevitable. It attached itself to Asfache — the one who found the tendrils and the one carrying it — and it rides on his back now. It is never wrong. It is never kind. It never volunteers anything. Which mattered, because when somebody finally thought to ask it how long they had, it answered immediately. It had been holding the number the entire time. Seventy-one hours until Tenebrosum finishes Callahan. The moment Innominandum died, Tenebrosum doubled its feeding to make up the loss. It knows when. It does not know why, and it says so.

95.title: Twelve hours in Wip
95.content: They could not walk at a Lieutenant like that. Casters dry, no long rest since before the Far Realm, six of them where there used to be nine. Resting in a convalescent Feywild was a gamble on time itself. So the gods carried them home to Wip — and then went their own ways. Thoth, Kratos, and Freya returned to the Edge of Existence. They will come to the Shadowfell the way they came to the Feywild: when Thoril calls them. Thoril went ahead to Mystica, alone, at half of what he was. Eldath carried Sofia to LIMA. And for twelve hours, the world got quiet.

96.title: Una gives away a piece of herself
96.content: Her father is still standing in a field in the Outlands. A creator god was mid-sentence when Thoth tore them out of the Dragonsmoot, and Una will not get back there inside seventy-one hours. So she found a magic item maker in Wip, handed over one of her own golden dragon scales, and commissioned a communication device out of it — to give Oman the next time she sees him, so that this never happens again. She has not finished it. She still has to reach him.

97.title: Asfache buys back fifteen years
97.content: In the timeline that no longer exists, he hatched Rodney and spent years turning him into a mount. The reset put the griffon back in the egg, and there was never going to be time to do it twice. So he spent fifteen years of his own Farylse time, and raised him in an afternoon. Rodney is a warmount now, in his prime, with decades in front of him. The fifteen years are gone. Farylse is closed forever. The rider got some work done too: R4 spent part of the same twelve hours reworking Asfache’s mechanical leg into a griffon’s.

98.title: Steven sees someone leave
98.content: He went to LIMA with Rat to sit with Sofia. There was an elf in white across the room, and she left the instant she saw him. He went after her and lost her. So he did the other thing — he asked around his own organization, the one he built, and came away with a name. Sienna. An elf volunteer at a lizardfolk aid house does not run from the man who founded it. Not unless she knows exactly who he is.

99.title: Rat stays
99.content: He was one of the two people who reached into Innominandum and pulled Sofia out. He sat down beside her and did not leave. She talks constantly, in something that is not a language. Thoth’s one gift to Rat is that he understands any language that is spoken. He has not mentioned it to anyone.

100.title: R4 blows up the Catty Shack
100.content: Smolder spent his one day off complaining about the competition. R4 listened, excused himself, went and got a La Bomba, and leveled the building.

101.title: Where that leaves them
101.content: Somewhere with no light in it at all: the Sunless Lake. And on the Astral, something drinks the Pool of Memories smaller. Roughly fifty-nine hours. Alamil’s circles can put them on Mystica within the hour — or so everyone believes this morning — and Catroniel is already there with Junish airships and a resistance army. From there: Albion, where a mad queen guards a Shadowfell portal and does not remember why. Then down into the deep Shadowfell, to a dry lakebed where light has never reached — the Sunless Lake — where the thing Sofia described as a tree with bark of shadow is inside Callahan himself, and is eating twice as fast as it was three days ago. She told them it went in through his mouth. She told them he has been screaming for months and nobody heard him. Those were close to the last words she had. Thoril has half a life left and every hour of it is already promised to that door. They are six. They have never done this before and they have already done it once. → Chapter 9: Chaos in Wip — a sabotaged circle, a missing wizard, and a dragon god on the roof.

103.doc: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
103.title: Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
103.content: A god’s errand finished at the front line, a party trick that saved a continent, and a robbery inside a painting. Thoth heard that they had Fate and Chaos both, and took them to the Edge of Existence. There is no useful way to describe it. An enormous fight, of incomprehensible size, in every direction, forever, with the gods in it. The party stood in the middle of that and waited while two deities had a conversation. Tyr would give up the Aspect of Order — if the mortals were worth it. So the party made their case. Una argued, and argued well. Asfache demonstrated. Smolder reasoned out the tactics of the thing in front of them, out loud, to the god of justice, and got listened to. Tyr handed the aspect over. Thoth performed the ritual on the spot: Fate and Chaos, bound through Order. What came out the other side was Truth. And the effect was immediate and absurdly simple. Every shapeshifter in the world now wore a thin purple-and-black aura, visible to anyone carrying the aspect’s power. Thoth granted it to all of them — and, better, made it transmissible, by the straightforward method of booping somebody on the forehead. The Boop of Truth. A year of paranoia, solved by poking people. Tap a forehead, see a shapeshifter. A continent’s worth of paranoia, solved by poking people.

104.doc: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
104.title: Bram remembers
104.content: They booped Bram, and his memories came back with everything else. He and his father had gone after the White Lion in Yore. They had been in the bushes, ready to strike. And a voice had sung: . “You will show where you’re hidden, Do as you’re bidden. Sing your songs no more, No sound, as before…” . Their hiding place stopped existing. They could not speak. And then: . “Back you go to friends and trade, Your memory here will wane and fade…” . Thoth listened to that and gave the party the only warning he had. The Lion Man is not a god. He is something outside of space and time, and Thoth did not know more than that. Be careful if you deal with him. Then he sent them back to Thoril’s tavern, and thanked them for finishing a quest the gods themselves had not managed.

105.doc: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
105.title: Thoril gets booped
105.content: They came back to find Thoril drunk and miserable again, so Smolder booped him with Truth. He straightened up like a man remembering an appointment. He was going to save his friends Marvin and Callahan, he said. Their essences are what keep the Feywild and the Shadowfell from collapsing. He thought he could help them. He gave Smolder a set of teleporting handwraps that had belonged to Marvin, wished them luck, and left in a burst of light.

106.doc: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
106.title: Flamencio
106.content: Then they went through his safes, because they are who they are. They were heavily warded, and while the party was working on them, a small man appeared in the middle of the tavern and announced that he would LOVE to paint them all. They had seen him once before, on Ancient Gamble Island. Flamencio helped with the wards on two of the safes in exchange for sitting. The safes gave up a very good shield and a pair of silk slippers; Sofia found a small chest in Thoril’s hop garden and planted a travel tree there while she was at it. And Flamencio painted each of them a 4x6 portrait, and while he worked, Bram asked him about the White Lion. Flamencio’s answer reframed the entire war for about ninety seconds. The White Lion is like him. Neither of them is a god, or a Far Realm thing, or anything with a name in anyone’s cosmology. They draw their power from the artistry of everything in existence, and there are quite a few of them, and collectively they call themselves The Artists. Flamencio paints things into being. The White Lion writes things into being. And Flamencio would happily take them to him. All they had to do was speak to the little paintings he’d just given them, and he would come.

107.doc: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
107.title: Wip, briefly
107.content: They went home through Sofia’s trees and spread the Boop of Truth through the city of Wip, and by the end of it roughly half of R4’s advisors were dead, because roughly half of R4’s advisors had been shapeshifters. They also picked up hearrings out of Newport — communication rings that work anywhere on the same plane, and have been standard party equipment ever since. Somewhere in the middle of all this, Bram turned into Bram Balls. He has never satisfactorily explained it. Bram Balls. Same-plane teleport charms, distributed liberally. Do not ask. Then they sat down with R4 and made a plan to go and get a writ out of a being that exists outside creation.

108.doc: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
108.title: The robbery
108.content: They spoke to their paintings, and Flamencio pulled them inside. They came out on a hill in a strange land with the White Lion waiting just beyond it. Bram went in disguised. And between Bram and Una, they talked him into it — the Lion agreed to write a writ that would silence the Siren Song, on one condition. The party had to perform in his new play. The Lion Who Shakes the Spear, keeping his word to people who had no intention of keeping theirs. Then an earthquake hit. The Lion dropped the writ and fell into a crevasse. The party took the writ and ran. They also understood perfectly well that you cannot hide from a being who exists outside space and time, and that he was going to come looking. So they did not wait for him. They planned an ambush, threw everything they had into getting the drop on him, and got it. They hacked off his limbs. Then his head. They left the torso where it lay and teleported back to Wip with the one object in existence that could shut Ghroth up. It is worth being honest about what that was. It was not a heroic act. It was a mugging, committed against something that had kept its word, by people who had run out of time to be nice. They were not wrong about needing it. → 2.9: The Muster — a year and a half in which everything went right.

109.doc: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
109.title: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear

110.title: Chaos in Wip
110.content: The morning they meant to leave, and nobody left. Where we are: Innominandum is dead. The Feywild is whole. Fifty-nine hours stand between Tenebrosum and the end of Callahan’s seal, and the plan is simple — step into Alamil’s circle, come out on Mystica, ride to Albion, go down into the dark. Every part of that plan is about to stop being true.

111.title: What Cat said
111.content: The Hearring call, before anyone had finished waking up. The message came through the Hearrings — the communication rings that work anywhere on the same plane — before anyone had finished waking up. Catroniel, from Mystica, with two things. The first: Thoril did not stay. He landed on that continent and he kept going. He is already inside the Shadowfell — alone, at half of what he used to be, with the other half already promised to a door, and he is not answering anyone. He can feel his friend dying and he has decided he is not going to be too late twice. Thoth, Kratos and Freya are still at the Edge of Existence. They will come to the Shadowfell the way they came to the Feywild — when Thoril calls them. Nobody can reach him to make sure he does. The second thing was smaller and stranger. “Tell R4’s wizard to stop running tests.” .

112.title: The circle
112.content: Ragar reads the circle. The Queen waits for the answer. R4 went to find Alamil. The room was empty. Nothing knocked over, nothing broken, nothing taken. A man who was there yesterday and is not there today. So R4 got Ragar instead, and Ragar looked at the teleport circle for a while, and then said the thing nobody wanted: . It has been tampered with since it was made. Not damaged. Not decayed. Altered. And whatever is written into it now, it will not put them where it says it will. He cannot tell them where it will put them. He cannot fix it. He said so plainly, and that is where it was left. Nobody has yet asked out loud whether “Alamil is gone” and “the circle is wrong” are two problems or one.

113.title: The Queen abdicates, sort of
113.content: The Outlands, after: one god, one empty field. R4 is about to leave the mortal plane on a deadline he might not come back from, wearing a dead woman’s face, ruling a city that does not know it. Luna Cantine came to find him. On the correct morning, at the correct hour, in front of the one person who had a problem she happened to be the answer to. She did not ask for anything. He made her intermediary Queen of Wip. The Matriarch of the Wolves. Head of the largest lycanthrope family in the city, one of the three heads of the Thieves Guild, and the single most capable operator on the council. She took it. Then he collected Una, used the Amulet of the Planes, and went back to the Outlands — to the field where the Dragonsmoot was abandoned mid-sentence. There was nobody in it. No dragons. No serpent gods. Not Bahamut, not Tiamat, not Kereska, not the serpent god Merrshaulk. Not Oman. Not Meiko. The greatest gathering of draconic power in ten thousand years had broken up and gone, and the god who called it was standing in an empty field by himself. He did not say where anybody had gone. R4 gave him a sending stone, to pass along to Oman, whenever IO manages to find him. IO took it. Nobody thought to ask a god standing alone in a field what had become of the assembly he called. Then they came back.

114.title: The council
114.content: They convened in the War Room in The Rock. Rat attended from LIMA, listening in through a Hearring. It went the way councils go. Grain, docks, guards, roads. Two things in it mattered. The first: the crater. Somebody had blown up the Catty Shack in the harbor district, and the council wanted an answer. Luna gave them one. Far Realm creatures. In the city, in the night, doing what Far Realm creatures do. Nobody at that table contradicted her. Including the Queen. Far Realm creatures, said the Matriarch of the Wolves. Nobody at that table had a better idea. The second: Mont Kiara. Ulaxium of the Arcane University has stopped responding. He has not answered a message in some time. In his place, the council keeps receiving messages — from six strange people. Who keep asking for “best friend.” . Smolder worked it out before anyone finished the sentence. Six people in one body is Ralf. And the best friend is him — he is the one who freed Ralf in this run, and it was not a small goodbye. Luna asked whether he would answer the next one. He said yes. The next one has not come.

115.title: Rat goes to the Beastlands
115.content: Rat before the Cat Lord, Felina, and the weather that judges. A panther walked into LIMA. Felina. She had walked R4 and Sofia through the Beastlands in the summer. She had sat with Sofia while Sofia talked about trees. She had liked her. She was there to summon Sofia to the Beastlands — the debt for the promise Sofia made in the summer, for the Fall, and could not keep, when the Cat Lord assembled the Mortai — the demigod-like cloud-beings of the Beastlands, the plane’s weather with a mind in it — on her word and was left standing in front of them. Rat showed her Sofia. Then he offered to go instead. They took the offer. He stood in front of the Cat Lord and the assembled Mortai for hours while they told him, in detail and at length and with no interruptions, precisely what had been done to them. He listened to all of it. Then he gave them an apology. It was not a perfect one. And then the Mortai moved on to the part of the rite that is not talking. The retribution nearly took him apart. He came back standing. What the Beastlands have decided about their armies, nobody has said.

116.title: Steven finds her
116.content: The Everscale changes hands. Word reached Steven that Sienna had been sighted, and he went, immediately, and did not stop. Sienna is Essyliss. They had it out. The vegetarian tenet, the Everscale, the argument at the Edge of Existence, all of it, in both directions, with Sofia lying a few feet away. And then they mended it. Not loudly. Nobody won it. Neither of them gave in, neither of them raised their voice, and at no point did a goddess descend or a prophet kneel. Two people who had hurt each other very badly said the true things out loud and were forgiven for them. Both of them wrote a new tenet. Steven’s is: .

117.title: “I am forgiven.”
117.content: Which is the only one of his ten that another person has to agree to. She agreed to it. Hers is: .

118.title: “I will not give up.”
118.content: Which is the only one of hers that nobody else gets a say in. And she gave the Everscale back. Nine surviving tenets, live again, for the first time since the day he handed it over. Then she told him the thing she had been carrying alone, the reason she was washing bandages in a volunteer house instead of standing with the World Serpent: . She thinks the fight against Ghroth is hopeless. She had gone and looked at Mappo No Ryujin with her own eyes. It had very nearly killed her. She had drawn her conclusion and she had been living inside it ever since. Steven told her about Innominandum. Six people. A lieutenant of Ghroth, dead in its own engine. And him, standing in the room when it happened. She changed her mind. She agreed to help him. And she agreed to try to do something for Sofia.

119.title: And then
119.content: The whole city heard the question. Steven and Una were walking back to The Rock when they saw them. A flight of chromatic dragons, coming in low over Wip. Then the sky went dark over the harbor and Tiamat landed on The Rock — on the building with the last Ley Crystal in the world inside it — and said, in a voice that every single person in that city heard at the same time: .

120.title: “WHERE IS HE?!”
120.content: They talked to her. They got the shape of it. She wants the Amulet of Null. Not the leg. Not an apology. Not a favor. The mark on Rat was only ever how she found the thief; it was never the thing she was owed. She has come for it, and she is standing on the roof until she gets an answer. And then she said the thing nobody expected her to volunteer. Her father sent her. IO dispatched her to find Null, and dispatched Bahamut to find Essyliss — the goddess Steven had found that same afternoon. She was not avenging a burglary. She was executing a commission, and she wanted them to know whose. Here is the answer nobody wants to say out loud: Rat sent Carxi to take it. Carxi gave it to Mordenkainen, in Avernus, who is at this moment using it — with his own future self’s spellbook — to open a way into the Null Realm as an escape hatch if the war is lost. Which risks the seal. Tiamat is one of the three who set that seal, alongside Asgorath and Bahamut. And the party is the only group of people in the cosmos who have already watched what happens when Null gets out: he rampaged, he killed gods at the Edge of Existence, and the war was lost. They cannot explain how they know that.

121.title: Where that leaves them
121.content: They asked her for a moment to talk it over. That moment is where we pick up. ⏱ Roughly forty-eight hours remain. Not one of the hours they spent today moved them a single step closer to Albion. The circle does not work. Alamil is gone, and the one wizard left in the city has already said he cannot fix what was done to the circle. Thoril is already down there in the dark by himself, and the gods are waiting on a man nobody can reach. There is a dragon god standing on their roof. And Smolder still owes somebody a reply. → Chapter 10: The Late Radtismir — the con that fooled a dragon god, and the war it bought them.

123.title: The Muster
123.content: A year and a half in which almost everything went right. From the fall of Year 2 to the summer of Year 3, the party stopped adventuring and started building, and it worked. The Boop of Truth spread outward from Wip city by city, taking Thoth’s following with it, and everywhere it went the shapeshifters stopped being invisible. Smolder’s Slums became an independent district under a deal with Liam, with a new Smut Shaq run by Bram’s sister Amelia. Rat and Carxi finally mended what killing her had broken — she gave him the Doshenkana poison and told him the tinkers had founded a town called Hemlock on the swamp’s edge to harvest poison components. Sofia awakened trees across the Land of Elements. R4’s goddess spoke to him and said she was proud of how many of their people he had freed, and that she would come to him in time. And Una went home. She confronted her mother about the infidelity, made her tell her husband the truth, and watched it go badly — which is what happens, and is also where healing starts. Her mother is now infatuated with Steven. Her father regards Steven as his nemesis. Nobody has resolved this.

124.title: The Arcane University
124.content: Then they geared up and flew to Mont Kiara to find out what had eaten a school. It was Ralf. The place was a maze of traps and taunts and — eventually, once everyone had stopped setting things off — a negotiation. What came out of it was a three-way agreement between Ralf, the party, and Meiko, the ancient gold dragon he had been holding: Ralf lets Meiko leave, and in exchange he gets access to all of her gems. Una closed it by returning Meiko’s golden dragon egg. The party got Skol Cantine freed as part of the same deal, which is the answer to a question Luna had been asking for a year. Una returned the egg. A three-way deal nobody trusted held together anyway. Una also finally got the books, and learned the rest of it: she is undergoing Dracogenesis. She will become a golden dragon. If she wants it, she should be able to change back. Meiko made her promise to look after the egg if Meiko fell at the Edge of Existence. And Ralf — who wanted the gems because he wanted to build La Bombas, as many as physically possible — asked the party for one thing in return. Go to the Starbold Hills, an extremely dangerous place, where there are creatures walking around with Ley Crystals implanted in them, and bring back as many crystals as they could carry. They left with a paper-thin alliance and a shopping list, and winter arrived.

125.title: Malachas
125.content: The Arch Fiend’s contact stone appeared in Rat’s workshop precisely two weeks and one minute after the deal in HIS Tower, exactly as advertised, and the news it brought was a whole new map. Two weeks and one minute, to the second. Arch Devils are punctual. The Blood War is over. The Demon Lord Amadread went missing. Without him the Abyss collapsed and the demons were enslaved. And on the other side of the ledger, Zariel — ruler of Avernus — vanished along with her senior archfiends, because they had all gone to fight at the Edge of Existence. That left a hole at the top of the Nine Hells, and something climbed into it. A rakshasa named Caspian. The same Caspian who had dealt magic items to the party in Wip. The same Caspian Asfache had killed at Mont Kiara — because a rakshasa killed on the mortal plane does not stay dead; it reforms in the Hells. He had gone home, and then he had taken the place over. Malachas wanted him gone, and wanted the party’s help doing it. That thread stayed live for the rest of the run. The interrogation of the devils who had stolen Rat’s poison book had already pointed the same way: Caspian is keeping tabs on you.

126.title: Winter and the third year
126.content: Una and Steven spent the whole winter brokering a real peace with the Fey and training with them, and came away knowing Misty Step. Freya contacted Smolder: the dragons of the Land of Elements have an old arrangement with the primordials and can grant their power, but he had to prove himself on the Field of Fire first. He did. Rat and Bram invented a holiday — the Winter Day of Reflection, on which people gather, boop each other, and give “Pennies for your Thoths” — and Thoth’s power grew accordingly. Alamil put a teleport circle on an airship, which is the kind of idea that seems obvious only afterwards. And Nyarlathotep came back and took the dwarven mountains again, so R4 started gathering an army. In the spring of Year 3 they used it. The party trained the muster, went in, and beat Nyarlathotep in both realms — the mortal one and the Far Realm it had twice escaped into. The Essylissian volunteers organized into LIMA and stayed behind to help rebuild the dwarven cities, with Steven, Bram and Asfache working the surrounding boar cities into the alliance. Una and Smolder ran the Field of Fire together and came out stronger for it. Rat got the poison farm at Hemlock running properly. Everybody missed Felafel that year. It is mentioned in the record with what can only be described as regret.

127.title: Summer, Year 3
127.content: The last full season before it all went wrong was the busiest of the run. Asfache, Una and Steven went into the Feywild and found it full of tarrasques and monstrosities, and helped Thoril rescue Marvin. Thoril told them what he had learned: the Feywild and the Shadowfell are going to close in the spring of Year 4. Rat took Ralf and Malachas into the Nine Hells and met Mordenkainen, who wanted a necklace of Tiamat’s in exchange for a legion of undead. They searched the Hells and they found it. R4 and Smolder cured Dryzzlazz at last, and then used her: they built a story that Freya can lift Llolth’s curses, and sent it into the Underdark to see what would bite. R4 also assembled a consortium of the world’s rulers into a single unified front, trained the combined force, and pushed Nephren-Ka — who had taken Hemlock and the swamp back — all the way to her tower. He got every nation on board except the Land of Elements, and sent people to learn how to ask them properly. Bram sang and storytold his way across Yore and convinced a third of the continent to fight. Smolder went into the Underdark himself. The well was empty. He dropped in, met the emissary and an escort, and then the tunnels flooded and the aboleths came. He got badly hurt and lost three quarters of the drow force he was traveling with. He reached the priestess of the city-state anyway. Meanwhile Alamil cut a portal to Yore for Bram, Ragar kept making La Bombas, and Luna and Skol organized the training of the largest army the world had assembled in living memory. The thieves came back from the west with a report nobody wanted. The land out there is overrun with shadow monsters. They were a year and two seasons from the deadline, with the writ in hand, the shapeshifters purged, the fey committed, an arsenal in production, and a continent under one banner. It was, by every measure they had, going well. → 2.10: The Amulet and the Edge — the theft, the release, and the battle they lost.

129.title: The Late Radtismir
129.content: The funeral of a living man, and the war it paid for. Where we are: Tiamat is standing on The Rock — on top of the last Ley Crystal in the world — demanding the Amulet of Null and asking for Rat by name. The party has asked her for a moment to confer. Roughly forty-eight hours remain on the Shadowfell clock, the teleport circles are sabotaged, and the road west now runs through people instead of doors. This is the moment they confer.

130.title: The promise
130.content: Una gave her the answer, speaking for all of them: we will hunt Rat down ourselves, and we will bring you the amulet. They named a meeting place — Sylvania, the party city in the Outlands — and five heads weighed the offer and found it acceptable. Then Tiamat left The Rock, and the city underneath it started breathing again — but just barely. The exhale. A down payment, not a pardon. Nobody said the other half of the plan out loud until she was gone.

131.title: The man who skipped his own funeral
131.content: First stop: the Beastlands, to tell Rat about his death. He heard the whole plan out. And then he said he would not be coming to it. Not out of fear — out of arithmetic. A senior Mortai attends Rat now: eight feet of slow grey weather with a face somewhere inside it, everywhere he goes, watching, saying nothing, reporting everything it sees to its seniors among the Mortai. It came back from the rite with him and it does not leave. Nobody stages the greatest fraud of their careers in front of the Beastlands’ idea of a court reporter. So the con of the Second Run went forward without its master thief, on his own instruction — which may be the most professional thing he has ever done. Rat stayed in the Beastlands, in front of the weather, doing nothing clever at all. Just showing it the things he actually holds to. Respect. Honesty. Honor. Whether weather can be impressed, weather does not say. It looked impressed. Rat and the weather. Nothing in his hands at all. And before he left, the Cat Lord gave him two things. An answer: the beasts of the Beastlands are committed to the war at the Edge of Existence — and whether the Mortai come too, the weather will decide for itself. And a bell: small, heavy, and not to be rung until the time comes to fight at the Edge.

132.title: The funeral arrangements
132.content: Second stop: Avernus, and the two people best positioned to build a corpse. Carxi heard the plan and grinned. Mordenkainen heard the plan, handed over the Amulet of Null, and got to work. He built them a body. Rat, to the last scar, cold on a slab. And onto it went the thing that has been riding in the real Rat’s bag of holding since Sylvania: the severed leg — the one still carrying the chromatic mark, the mark Tiamat has followed across two planes. The mark is how she finds her thief. From that moment on, her own tracking would swear the thief was exactly where the party said he was. Mordenkainen builds a body; Carxi is having a lovely time. The leg is the part that sells it. Before they left, they gave the archmage a second job: go to Wip and look at the broken teleport circles. Mordenkainen and Carxi went.

133.title: Limbo, and a stranger
133.content: Limbo. Where the ground does not agree with itself from one minute to the next, and where a falling rock needs no explanation. That is where Rat died. Crushed, tragically, mid-escape, fleeing from the party that had hunted him down, the stolen amulet still among his effects. A story with everything in it: a chase, a thief, justice, gravity. Asfache and Smolder stayed with the corpse, keeping the scene honest, and a bit awkward. And while they stood their strange vigil, they noticed they were being watched. Something in the churn was watching, and had been for a while. Asfache went after it. The chase ended the way Asfache’s chases end. What he caught was a githzerai — gaunt, wrapped, entirely composed about being caught — whose first words were an allegiance check: did Asfache serve the githyanki, or the mind flayers? . Asfache told him the truth. He does not serve mind flayers. He kills them. He has split an elder brain in half with his own hands. A warrior, a modron, and a githzerai who was supposed to be watching from a great deal further away. The githzerai considered this. Then he gave his name — Dak’kon — and asked for their help. With what, he has not yet said. But he left something behind: a paper roll, instructions to his githzerai city, written in Deep Speech and Gith. An invitation, with an address, in two scripts nobody present could read. He is, presumably, expecting them.

134.title: The long way to Sylvania
134.content: Meanwhile Una, R4 and Steven took the Amulet of the Planes and went to collect a dragon god. The amulet had opinions. It put them in Fortitude, in the Outlands. Then it put them in a mirror dimension, where something gangly and slender and almost shaped like a man was present, and they did not linger. Then it put them on Pirate Isle, on the mortal plane, briefly and without explanation. Then, at last, grudgingly: Sylvania, where Tiamat was waiting, as promised.

135.title: The handover
135.content: They led her to Limbo. To a rock, and to what was under it. Five heads considered the scene, and every piece of it agreed with every other piece. The corpse with Rat’s face. The leg with her mark still burning in it. The Amulet of Null, recovered from a dead thief’s effects — exactly as promised, exactly on time. She took it. Corpse, mark, and amulet — every piece agreeing with every other piece. She left satisfied. And then she looked at Una — the newest gold dragon in the world, the one who had made the promise and kept it to the letter — for slightly too long, and said: .

136.title: “I’ll be keeping an eye on you.”
136.content: And then she was gone, her brother’s prison in her claws, believing Rat dead. The most dangerous object in the cosmos, treated as a receipt.

137.title: Two verdicts in Wip
137.content: Back in Wip, Mordenkainen had an answer about the circles, and it was worse than the question. They go to Avernus. All of them. Someone reworked the network so that every circle on the continent delivers its passengers to the Nine Hells — carefully, and deliberately. It is a trap, and it was built for this party. He can fix it, he says. It would take him about a year. Without Alamil. Against the clock they are living on, that is a no with extra steps. But it is the first time the door west has come with a price instead of a refusal. And at LIMA, Steven looked in on Sofia — and found two goddesses arguing over her bed. Essyliss and Eldath, mid-disagreement, at whisper volume, about how to heal her. The idea on the table: forcefully wildshaping her. A new shape. A fresh body. Neither goddess would promise it brings her mind back. Steven said he would talk to the party first. No decision has been made.

138.title: Six letters and a mountain
138.content: And then, at last, the message came for Smolder. Six of them, actually. One from each of Ralf’s personalities, each contradicting the other five. Reading them in sequence was like hearing an argument through a wall. So they went up Mont Kiara to have the argument in person — and found the Arcane University under attack. Devils and demons at the doors. And holding the doors against them: students. Dozens of students, moving with the same instincts, covering the same angles, because Ralf has been embedding his mind into the students and teachers. Dozens of students, one set of instincts, and Ralf taking notes through all of it. And in the middle of it all, Ralf. All six of him, in one body. Who finally explained what the letters could not agree on: . Caspian has made him an offer. A body for each personality. Six minds, six bodies, nobody sharing, ever again. Some of the Ralfs want it more than they have ever wanted anything. Some of them would rather die as one than live as six. The contract arrives tomorrow.

139.title: The counteroffer
139.content: The party talked it over, and their position on the contract came together very fast: . If the counterparty — Caspian — is dead before the ink arrives, there is nothing to sign. Ralf armed them himself — La Bombas, from the mountain Caspian has spent two years scheming to acquire, handed over by the wizard he is trying to buy, to the people now delivering them at speed. Then a contact stone that had waited a very long time finally got used, and Malachas answered. The Arch Devil has wanted Caspian gone since the throne of Avernus was stolen out from under everyone. He did not need persuading. He brought forces. He brought intelligence. He found the target: . Caspian is aboard Zariel’s old flagship, flying over Avernus. Mordenkainen teleported everybody to the war — everybody: with Tiamat well and truly gone, Rat rejoined his own “mourners” for the assault. So that is what rose through the burning sky of the Nine Hells toward a warship: six adventurers — one of them officially deceased — one modron, one archmage, one extremely pleased thief, an Arch Devil, and his assembled host. The ship opened fire.

140.title: Where that leaves them
140.content: That is where the session ended, and that is where the next one starts: mid-air, mid-barrage, over Avernus. ⏱ Roughly thirty hours remain. The road west is open again, barely — an archmage who can carry them, an amulet that gambles — while the circle network stays dead until somebody spends a year on it, or rescues Alamil. Thoril is still down in the dark alone, and three gods still wait on a call only he can make. The contract still lands at Mont Kiara tomorrow. A githzerai’s scroll sits untranslated in somebody’s pack. A vote about Sofia is waiting for a quieter hour that may not come. And somewhere in that boarding party, a bell in his pocket, the late Radtismir is very carefully staying dead in the middle of a war.

142.title: The Amulet and the Edge
142.content: The theft, the release, and the battle they lost. Autumn of Year 3 opened with the harvest of everything they had planted. The Fey were evacuating the Feywild and had formally agreed to fight at the Edge of Existence. The alliance held. The armies were training. The arsenal was stacking up. And then the portals started opening. Feywild portals, spilling monstrosities and displaced fey. Shadowfell portals, spilling shadow creatures. The two mirror planes were failing on schedule, and the schedule had never been a secret. The party split up one last time to finish their errands. Asfache had Rodney trained at last, and went to R4 about his leg — the one the tarrasque took in the Feywild, which Steven’s bone leg had been standing in for — and came away with a new one, made of metal, which took some getting used to. He also went to the Land of Elements and learned they could not be brought to the Edge of Existence, and came back to say so. R4 built Asfache’s leg, and then built Una a golden eye to go under a golden eyepatch — out of shapechanger skin — and in doing so cracked the last of the problem he had been working on since the beginning. Warforged could now be given shapeshifting skin. Warforged shapeshifters exist now, because he made them. Steven grew LIMA into something closer to a volunteer army, and taught people to craft from an inventory of his own detachable body parts. Sofia went into the woods and awakened everything in them — squirrels, birds, badgers — and came back with an army of woodland creatures. Bram did a lookbook for the Smut Shaq in Glarsht, which he would like noted in the record. Smolder finished the Underdark. He reached the Priestess of Llolth, gave the sight of shapeshifters to a lowly drow male, and had him boop the priestess. She saw what was standing in her own temple and ordered the shapeshifters seized, and the city came apart. He walked out of the pandemonium with a deal to introduce Dryzzlazz to the Matron Mother and a battalion to escort him home. And Rat went to Avernus.

143.title: The tomb
143.content: Tiamat’s tomb. He got in, went around every guardian the place had, and came out with the Amulet of Null. Almost. On the way, something got a claw into him — a shadowy dragon, one of the vault’s own wards, that scratched him once and left a mark he would carry across two timelines. In, around every guardian, and out with the amulet. Almost clean. He took the amulet to Mordenkainen’s tower, then traded Malachas a hammock for a ride back to the mortal plane. That is the whole crime. A successful heist, professionally executed, by the best thief in the world, against a hoard whose owner was away at a war.

144.title: The release
144.content: Half the party met in the war room. They sent Ralf to raid Mordenkainen for his notes on Null — the archmage, they later understood, had his own plans for the amulet: a refuge carved out inside the Null Realm, or a ransom paid to Bahamut for it. He meant to watch the coming battle with Ghroth rather than be caught in it. Then the amulet touched the mortal plane. Null, loose in the world for the first time in an age, arriving somewhere that had not been expecting him. Null the Dragon God was freed. He did not kill the party. He barely noticed them. He tore The Rock open on his way out, and then he flew to the Edge of Existence and began settling accounts with his family — and with everything standing near them. He killed gods. The divine line that had been holding Ghroth’s forces back for years, already stretched to nothing, came apart from behind. Ghroth’s forces took the advantage and did not give it back. Every plan Mordenkainen had for that amulet ended in the same moment. The party had spent three years and three seasons building a war they could win, and they lost the war in an afternoon, to a burglary.

145.title: The gamble
145.content: So they chose the one thing left that was still theirs to choose: when. The last Ley Crystal still had over a year of power in it. If they waited, Ghroth would arrive at full strength against a divine line that was already broken and getting worse. So they broke the crystal themselves. They destroyed the Wip Ley Crystal, forced Ghroth to come early, and moved the entire assembled army to the Edge of Existence through Sofia’s grove — every ally, every city, every alliance of five years, walking through a tree onto the worst battlefield in creation. The road to the Edge of Existence. Everyone on it had been told how the odds ran.

146.title: The song
146.content: Ghroth arrived, grotesquely, and began to sing. There was a gap — a few seconds, no more — between the first note and Steven getting the writ up. In that gap the Siren Song rolled over the whole army, and the whole army heard it. The Far Realm rewrote what it touched. Steven’s teeth changed into something that offers him more power if he eats meat. Asfache grew eyes all over his head. Sofia was given a frog sac in her throat that swells and retracts on its own. Hundreds of soldiers were changed in hundreds of ways. It was not an attack; it was an edit. Then Steven raised the writ of the White Lion, and the song stopped. It worked. The single hardest problem the gods had set them, the thing five years of work had been aimed at, and it worked exactly as advertised, on the day, in front of everybody. Five years of work, one sheet of paper, and it did exactly what it said on the day. And then the Three Lieutenants came down — Innominandum, Mappo No Ryujin, Tenebrosum — and the line broke, and the battle went badly, and then quickly, and then it was over.

147.title: The scroll
147.content: There was one thing left in the bag. Two years earlier, in a lich’s tower, they had looted a maze full of traps for anything that wasn’t nailed down, and among the loot had been a scroll nobody could use. It had sat there, unregarded, through a primordial and a paint-portal and a war. A Time Travel Scroll. They read it, and wound the world back to the beginning of the Five-Year Prep — to the morning after the gods came in a dream, with everything ahead of them again, and the whole of it already in their heads. They did not arrive quietly. Something noticed a timeline being edited, and came for them in their sleep. → Chapter 3: Farylse & the Chronologians — the arrest, the deal, and a shattered plane where time is terrain.

149.title: Aditi
149.content: Goddess of Consciousness. Patron of R4. Aditi is revered by the warforged, and R4 is her Champion. What she gives him is the sharing of consciousness — the ability to reach and touch another mind — and he has built an entire political career on it. Known for. Gaining strength from R4’s warforged liberation at the Statue of the Wanderer in Gaiadon, where the inert warforged were freed and woken. What her absence is like. In the Far Realm, R4 was cut off from her completely: deaf to every living mind he had spent two years cultivating, alone inside his own head for the first time since the day he woke up — and still the one everybody looked to.

150.title: Gallery
150.content: The waking at the Statue of the Wanderer. A hall of lamps that had never been lit, and a goddess who grew stronger with every one of them.

151.title: Alamil
151.content: Portal mage. Information broker. The party’s fast travel — and the party’s missing person. Alamil is a teleportation specialist and an information broker, and for two years he has been the reason this party can be in two places on the same day. Wip, Halos, Gaiadon, and one aboard the airship: he built them all, at a pace the art is not supposed to allow. He is also, quietly, the man who told them what they were fighting. After the ziggurat it was Alamil who explained Ghroth to R4 — a giant eye in the Far Realm; a horde that mimics people perfectly; Ley Crystals repel them; and the crystal in Wip has about five years left in it. Every plan the party has made since is downstream of that conversation. Then he wasn’t there. R4 went to his room on the morning of the Wip chaos and found it empty. Nothing knocked over. Nothing taken. No sign of anybody leaving in a hurry, and no sign of anybody leaving at all. Ragar examined the circle that same morning and found it had been tampered with since it was made — and could not fix it. Mordenkainen later put a price on the repair: about a year of his work, without Alamil’s help. That is the measure of the man. The best archmage available quotes a year to replace what one portal mage does for a living. The lock and the key went missing in the same hour, and nobody has decided out loud what that means. He is a man who could have opened every door on the continent, and the party still does not know whether he was taken, bought, or simply told to go. Where he stands now. Missing. The ledger’s line for him is the plainest thing on it: Alamil is still missing, and now worth a network.

152.title: Chronologian Arch-Knights
152.content: The Chronologians’ heavy elite. . The Arch-Knights are what the Chronologians send when the matter is settled and only the enforcement is left. Gold plate, a faceless helm, and a clockwork sigil at the breast; they arrive inside a storm of turning gears and hanging clock faces, and they fight the way a verdict fights. The party met them in the Chronologian stronghold, on the way to Damian Heath — with Mordenkainen in the line beside the party and Freya still in a cell somewhere ahead. There is a coda to this, in Farylse: out on the broken time-terrain the party came across a gigantic statue of a man armored like the time cops, standing over a plane where time is landscape. Nobody has explained it.

153.title: Asfache
153.content: Warrior, lycanthrope. Champion of Kratos, Seer of the Pool. Asfache fights for Kratos and rides a griffon named Rodney. He united the fire clans and took the Field of Fire, and he is the reason Caspian died the first time — one devastating critical hit at Mont Kiara, years ago. The eyes. Ghroth’s Siren Song left him with eyes that will not stop seeing. In the Far Realm this was the exception that won the fight: inside the false beauty of Innominandum’s works, every seam showed itself to him the instant it formed. It was Asfache who spotted the governor tendrils still trailing off the torn-out controls and called the whole party onto them — the play that let six people take hold of the engine together and pin the Lieutenant for the kill. He paid for it in constant psychic overload, and he cannot un-see any of it. The Pool. His dreams of the Pool of Memories and a green orb led, in Sylvania, to uniting the doll and the orb — and the forgotten god inside gained partial awareness and named the giant robot as its body. Asfache can now see the Pool, and watch it shrink. He left the orb at the Far Realm threshold, watched Cal dissolve for the second time, and went in anyway. Where he stands now. Pentad-Nine, the Mechanus modron that came back with the party, rides on his back and answers to him. He spent fifteen years of his own Farylse time aging Rodney into a full warmount in an afternoon. On corpse-duty in Limbo he caught a githzerai spying, ran him down, and was asked “githyanki, or mind flayers?” — the answer earned a name, Dak’kon, and a request for help. He is riding Rodney into the assault over Avernus.

154.title: Gallery
154.content: Asfache and Rodney, back when Rodney was still a fledgling and an afternoon in Farylse had not yet aged him fifteen years. The Land of Elements. He united the fire clans, took the Field of Fire, and had a drink about it. *“You get an orange, you get an orange!” — the Champion of War, distributing morale.* . A franchise. Of course it is a franchise. *“Ya bolstered with smoothies!” Support, as practiced by the god of war’s own.* . *“Ya bolstered!” The whole party has heard this. Most of them were bleeding at the time.* . The Feywild, First Run. A tarrasque took the leg. The artist’s version is smaller and no less pleased with itself. The replacement, First Run: in the field, out of what was lying about. It held. Steven did the fitting, First Run. Neither of them stopped to ask whether it was a good idea. Asfache, as the dice see him. Asfache and Kratos. It has never been a subtle relationship. Pentad-Nine rides on his back and answers to him. Nobody has satisfactorily explained why. Corpse-duty in Limbo: one modron, one warrior, and the githzerai who had been watching them for rather too long.

155.title: Astridia
155.content: Oversees her own timeline, and leads the Council of Eternity. Above the time cops sits the Council of Eternity — the body that actually governs time — and at the head of the Council sits Astridia. The party has never met her. They are nonetheless already inside her business, because the deal Damian Heath offered them is aimed directly at her. If they beat Ghroth, he collects them; and what he wants them for is upsetting the balance of power on a council he sits on and cannot outvote. The war against the Siren is, from a certain angle, an opening move in somebody else’s much longer war.

156.title: What she trades in
156.content: Farylse is the clearest look anyone has had at how she works. The doors of that plane are kept by people who made a deal with Damian Heath or with Astridia, and who now guard, forever, the thing they bargained for. General Gloom is the example that stays with you. He carried an entire city and its armies out of Ghroth’s path on the backs of the Palanquin titans, arrived in Farylse with everything he had saved, and watched it become the other strange things in that place. Astridia offered to numb the pain if he would keep her portal. He took it. Her reach is not confined to dead plane-corners either: the Circle of Elders on Eara and their meddling with the timeline lead back toward her. Where she stands now. Distant, enormous, and busy elsewhere. She has not looked at the party yet. That is the best news on this page.

157.title: Bahamut
157.content: King of the metallic dragons. One of IO’s two great extensions. Currently searching every plane in creation for a woman who is folding blankets in Steven’s headquarters. Bahamut is the metallic half of dragonkind, to Tiamat’s chromatic half — the second of the three extensions IO broke into, and the one who is generally assumed to be on the right side of things. The two of them have not been in the same field for a very long time, and there is nothing left to mediate between them: the binding force of the World Serpent is missing, which is precisely why the Dragonsmoot ran as hot as it did. The party never got a private word with him. What they got was the tension — palpable from as far away as Sylvania, where every dragon passing through split along factional lines even while drinking together.

158.title: What he saw at the Dragonsmoot
158.content: Una. When the Breath of Becoming finished what IO’s arrival had started, Bahamut looked at the newly forged gold and saw the metallic ideal made flesh — a dragon born out of devotion and choice rather than blood alone. Tiamat, standing across the same field, saw something considerably more alarming. Both of them have taken a direct interest in her since. What either intends to ask of her, nobody knows.

159.title: The errand
159.content: IO sent Tiamat to find Null, and Bahamut to find Essyliss. The party did not hear this from either god — Tiamat told them herself when she landed on The Rock. So the King of the Metallic Dragons is at this moment quartering the planes for the missing binding force of the World Serpent, on his father’s commission, with the full weight of the metallic host behind him. Steven found her first. She was in an aid station wearing an elf’s face, under the name Sienna, and she has been there the whole time. Where he stands now. Still looking. He does not know he has been beaten to it, and the party has not gone out of its way to tell him. Bahamut is one of only six dragons alive who could recognize Rat’s face. He is also one of the four who would not mention it to his sister.

160.title: Baz Stricknaz
160.content: Bastard prince of Jun. Killed at Saki. Still following Bram. Baz Stricknaz was a hobgoblin, the bastard son of King Ramses Jun, and an ambitious commander who had worked out that a private army is mostly a paperwork problem. He raised one on forged royal writs and was well on the way to being a serious question for the kingdom. Bram answered the question at the Battle of Saki, with a knife to the throat, while Willamet, Baz’s half-brother, was still trying to heal Baz. And Baz cursed him with the last thing he had. The shadows took the body where it lay — no corpse, nothing left behind but his gear — and what stood up out of it was not Baz any more, or not only. He is a ghost and a reaper at once, barely in control of himself, and he has exactly one interest. He follows the party’s shadows, and he is dead set on Bram. By the curse’s own rule the debt runs one way: only Bram can put him down for good. At the Jun Ziggurat, when Ramses — his father — went down gravely wounded in front of him, the reaper-shadow lost whatever was left of its composure entirely and attacked everyone in the room while the ceiling came down on all of them. Bram is currently away on Väinämöinen’s business, unreachable, and sendings do not connect. The thing hunting him has no such difficulty. Where he stands now. On the ledger under Enemies, listed as Baz’s Reaper, waiting in the dark for the one person who can end him to come back into the light.

161.title: Bram
161.content: Bard of Yore. Väinämöinen’s man, the one who killed a prince. Bram — Bram Balls — is the party’s bard and storyteller, out of the Ash family of traveling performers, with deep ties to the plane of Yore and a brother named Otto the 7th. His patron is Väinämöinen, a god who lost his voice to the White Lion. Known for. The Bram Balls themselves: same-plane teleport charms, distributed liberally and responsible for more of the party’s logistics than anyone likes to admit. The White Lion quest — the search that produced the writ to silence the Siren Song, twice: once by force in the First Run, and once by trade in Farylse, when the Lion turned out to have survived being hacked apart (Artists cannot truly be killed) and wanted his own body parts back. The prince. In Saki, at the very beginning, the party turned on Baz Stricknaz — bastard prince of Jun, host to a Reaper — and it was Bram who put the knife to his throat. Baz died cursing. His shadow swallowed his own corpse, and what stood up was a ghost-and-reaper hybrid made of rage. Where he stands now. Baz hunts Bram through the party’s shadows, relentless and patient. Bram is the only one who can land the killing blow and end it permanently. Baz only needs to catch him once.

162.title: Gallery
162.content: Bram Balls. Same-plane teleport charms, distributed liberally. Do not ask. The other one in the room. He plays facing the crowd. There is a reason for that, and the crowd has never once noticed it.

163.title: Callahan
163.content: The third of the three. The Shadowfell’s seal. The clock. Callahan helped kill Orcus, with Thoril and Marvin, and then did what Marvin did: he sealed his own soul into a plane to hold the walls of the world apart. Marvin took the Feywild. Callahan took the Shadowfell. Marvin was fed on. Callahan is being inhabited. Tenebrosum is not standing on his seal. It is inside him — it went in through the mouth — and the intelligence Sofia paid everything to bring back includes the detail nobody wanted: he has been screaming for months. Every number in this war is him. The seventy-one hours were not the Shadowfell’s deadline in the abstract; they were the time until Callahan is consumed, and the plane falls when he does. The ledger does not even bother phrasing it as a plane any more. Thoril owes him the other half of a life. Half went into Marvin’s seal in the Feywild. The rest is for Callahan’s door, and Thoril has already crossed into the dark alone to spend it. He has never spoken to the party. Everything they know about him has arrived second-hand: through Sofia’s dying report, through a schedule kept by a modron, and through Thoril, who can feel him breaking from another plane and describes it like a man listening through a wall. Where he stands now. At the bottom of the Sunless Lake, in the deep Shadowfell, on a clock with roughly thirty hours left on it.

164.title: Carxi
164.content: “Catsclaw.” Catroniel’s lieutenant, then Rat’s protégé. Currently on a burning ship, extremely pleased. Carxi — Catsclaw — is a gnome who came up under Catroniel and has spent the Second Run being handed the jobs nobody else can be told about. In Year 1 she scouted HIS Swamp and came back saying she needed an army, which was correct. Then there were two of her. In the First Run she scouted the same swamp, and moments after she delivered that report a shapeshifter wearing her face walked up behind her. The identification spell failed. So the party did the only arithmetic available to them: they killed both and resurrected the one they wanted. She came back knowing exactly what her friends had decided about her, with a specificity that most people never have to face. It took a year and a half to fix, and it did get fixed — by the time of the muster she was pressing the Doshenkana poison into Rat’s hand herself. In the Second Run she has been the quiet solution. Rat sent her pre-emptively to handle the Amulet of Null — she lifted it out of Tiamat’s horde earlier and far more quietly than the First Run heist managed — and delivered it to Mordenkainen in Avernus. Carxi heard the plan and grinned. She and Mordenkainen built the counterfeit corpse that convinced a dragon god that Rat was dead. Then she went to Wip with him to read the circles, and then she went to the war. Where she stands now. Aboard Zariel’s flagship over Avernus, described in the dispatches as one extremely pleased thief.

165.title: Caspian
165.content: Rakshasa. Dealmaker. Currently the owner of Avernus, and currently being shot at. Caspian is a rakshasa, which means he has never once needed to be in the room. He began as a dealmaker in Wip — magic items, favors, introductions — and every deal turned out to be a step in a procurement chain that nobody noticed he was walking. The First Run paper trail is the clearest picture of him anyone has, and the party read it themselves through Smolder’s Robe of Eyes: he traded 150 igloids to Prodigy Melts for a “Magic Bomb” spell, and he took Alissa Locksheed hostage in a mirror to get himself into the Arcane University at Mont Kiara. The party beat him there. Asfache then killed him at Mont Kiara with a critical hit, which turns out to be a temporary condition for his kind. In the Second Run he took Avernus — walked into the vacuum Zariel left when she went to fight at the Edge of Existence, and stayed. From there he has been watching. Every member of the party has a glowing orb following them, relayed by enslaved wizards on the material plane, and his stated intent has always been the same: strike when they are weakest. Two things went wrong for him this month. R4 leveled his Catty Shack with a La Bomba because Smolder was annoyed about the competition. And every teleport circle on the continent turned out to deliver to Avernus — Mordenkainen named it as a trap built for this party, which is the moment the party stopped guessing who they were dealing with. Then he made his offer. At Mont Kiara he put a contract in front of Ralf: a body of his own for each of the six personalities. The contract arrives tomorrow. Where he stands now. The party’s answer to the contract was not a counter-offer. They took La Bombas from Ralf, used Malachas’s contact stone, and went to Avernus to kill the counterparty before the ink lands. He is aboard Zariel’s old flagship, over Avernus, and the ship has opened fire. Still riding on the outcome: the scrying orbs, and a contract due at Mont Kiara in the morning.

166.title: The Cat Lord & Felina
166.content: The Beastlands sent a panther, and then it sent a bill. Felina is a panther, and she is the friendly half of this. She walked R4 and Sofia through the Beastlands in the summer, sat with Sofia while she talked about trees, and liked her. Sofia promised to come back in the Fall. She did not come back. By the Fall, Sofia was catatonic on a cot at LIMA and could not have been carried to a doorway, let alone through one. And in the Beastlands, on Sofia’s word, the Cat Lord had already assembled the Mortai — the demigod-like cloud-beings of the Beastlands, the plane’s weather with a mind in it — and was left standing in front of them with nothing to say. So Felina came to LIMA to collect. She found Rat sitting beside Sofia, where he had been for twelve hours. He showed her the body, and then offered to go in Sofia’s place. They took it. What followed was hours of admonishment before the Cat Lord and the assembled Mortai, an apology that was true and not quite complete — and then the retribution, which very nearly took Rat apart. He came back standing. The verdict came from the Cat Lord himself, in person, and it is the second-largest muster of the Second Run: the beasts of the Beastlands are committed to the Edge of Existence. Whether the Mortai come is a separate question, and it is the Witness’s to answer. And then he gave Rat a bell. Small, heavy, unremarkable to look at. It is not to be rung for a favor, an emergency, or a war. It is to be rung when the time comes to fight at the Edge of Existence, and it will be answered. A summoning instrument for an army, in the pocket of a man who is currently, officially, dead.

168.title: Catroniel
168.content: Gnome. Rat’s mentor and adopted brother. Dead for a whole run, and currently holding Mystica. Catroniel — Cat — taught Rat everything, founded the Ghostbloods, and lost an arm and a leg in the Gamble Island disaster. He is the reason Rat is who he is, and for the entire First Run he was not there. The party never met the real Cat in the First Run. A shapeshifter wore his face for the whole of it, including the emotional reunion in the Heartforge — the forge in The Rock — that everybody believed. Killing that imposter is where Dark Rat came from — his lowest moment, the hour the imposter was revealed — and it is the single worst thing that has ever happened to the party’s spymaster. The Second Run fixed it, in the pettiest possible order. Rat walked into the Last Leg Casino on rebuilt Gamble Island, where the proprietor had mounted Cat’s skeletal arm beside the door as a signpost — this way for good times — with Cat’s ring still on it. Rat took the ring for nothing, because Cat had trained him never to pay more than five percent of a first ask. The ring turned out to be a Ring of X-Ray Vision, which is how he found the rest of the skeleton buried two feet under the front step. He reversed the body’s decay with time magic, carried it into Thoril’s bar in the middle of Thoril’s own revelation, and Steven put the soul back in. Then Cat went straight back to work. He went into the Feywild with Rat, Una, Sofia and Thoril, fought the Tarrasque, and flew deeper to find Innominandum. He now commands the resistance in Mystica against the shadow creatures, with airships on loan from the Junish Army. The ledger’s line for him is three words: Cat holds the line. And he is the one who called. The Wip chaos day started with Cat on the other end of Rat’s Hearring with two facts: Thoril has already crossed into the Shadowfell, and “tell R4’s wizard to stop running tests.” Nobody has yet worked out what the second one means — only that Cat is at the far end of a network somebody else was using. Where he stands now. Mystica, in the dark, with the west resting on him. Restored, re-armed, and the only friendly eye anywhere near Thoril.

169.title: Gallery
169.content: Before Gamble Island. Two hands, two legs, and a con that had run five weeks without incident.

170.title: The Chronologians
170.content: You do not rewind five years of history without somebody noticing. The Chronologians — time cops — intercepted the party’s jump, took Freya, and lost a running battle through their own stronghold. Their leader, Damian Heath, did not want to stop the party. He wanted to use them, and the deal he offered is still outstanding. Above the time cops sits the Council of Eternity, and at the head of it sits Astridia — whose balance of power is the thing Damian’s deal is pointed at. Beyond his gate lay Farylse, where time is terrain rather than current, and where the party met, among much stranger company, a woman in a crown who is now standing between them and the Shadowfell. Damian Heath — The time cop who let the party go. Arch-Knights — The heavy elite of temporal law. Timecops — The rank and file. The Mad Queen of Albion — Met in Farylse. Now in the doorway. Astridia — Head of the Council of Eternity. Distant.

171.title: Dak’kon
171.content: Githzerai. Caught watching. Asked for help and did not say with what. Dak’kon is a githzerai — gaunt, wrapped, and entirely composed about the fact that he had just been caught. He was watching Asfache and Smolder in Limbo while they stood vigil over a corpse. Asfache noticed something in a plane where nothing holds still holding perfectly still, ran him down, and caught him. His first words were not an apology. They were an allegiance check: did Asfache serve the githyanki, or the mind flayers? . Asfache’s answer was a résumé. He has killed illithids. He has split an elder brain in half with his own hands. The interrogation stopped being an interrogation somewhere in the middle of that sentence and became a request. He gave his name and asked for help. With what, he has not said. And he left them a paper roll: instructions to his city, written in Deep Speech and Gith — two scripts that nobody standing in Limbo that day could read. Deep Speech is the aberrations’ own tongue. Nobody has yet asked why a githzerai’s directions home are written in half of it. Where he stands now. Unknown. Somewhere on the other end of a document the party is carrying and cannot read, presumably waiting to hear whether they are coming.

173.title: Damian Heath
173.content: Leader of the Chronologians. The man who let the party go. Damian Heath leads the Chronologians and sits on the Council of Eternity — the body that governs time itself. He is the steward of this timeline, and he is bitterly tired of stewarding one that is doomed to fail. When the party wound the world back five years, his people intercepted the jump. The party fought their way through a Chronologian stronghold alongside Mordenkainen, freed Freya from Chronologian custody, and were brought at last in front of him. He did not want to stop them. He wanted to use them. The terms: he releases the party and Freya to go and defeat Ghroth. If they succeed, he recruits them to upset the balance of power inside the Council of Eternity. If they fail, they die, and he remains steward of a doomed timeline exactly as before. He had nothing to lose by letting them try. The party took the deal. Where that leaves them. Winning against Ghroth means Damian comes to collect, and the party goes to war for him inside the Council. Losing is the only way out of the contract, and losing has its own drawbacks.

174.title: Gallery
174.content: The offer. He had nothing to lose by letting them try, and he has never once looked worried about the answer.

175.title: Dragons & the World Serpent
175.content: A raspy, broken voice called every dragon in creation to one field in the Outlands — the first Dragonsmoot in ten thousand years — and told them he intends to put the World Serpent back together. It cannot currently be done. The binding force is missing, and one of IO’s own three extensions is sealed inside an amulet. So the greatest assembly of draconic power in an age listened, dispersed, and went off on errands nobody explained. One of them landed on The Rock afterwards and asked the city a question. The party has one of them in the family. IO (Asgorath) — Called them all. Then stood in the field alone. Tiamat — Came for the amulet. Got it. Bahamut — Searching the planes for a goddess who has already been found. Null — The third dragon god. Sealed. Meiko — Ancient gold. Went recruiting. Not back. Oman — Una’s father. The flame she was forged in. Kereska — Dragon goddess of magic. Knew the old rite. Vessa — Copper chronicler. Smelled the receipt.

177.title: Dryzzlazz
177.content: Drow drider. The Spiders of the Wip Thieves Guild. Cured of the madness in both runs; the legs stayed. Dryzzlazz runs the Spiders, one of the three houses of Wip’s Thieves Guild — alongside Luna Cantine’s Wolves and Aegor’s Moles. When the party first walked into a besieged Wip, the city’s underworld was the only machinery still functioning, and hers was one third of it. She was also cursed — a drow twisted into drider form and driven mad with it. The party cured the madness; the drider body is hers to keep. Then, in the Second Run, knowing exactly what was wrong and exactly how to fix it, they cured her again, years earlier, and got a functioning ally out of the years they saved. She has served since as the party’s contact into Drow politics, which is a heavier job than it sounds in a run where Smolder has been settling Underdark disputes by assassination. The Spider Queen is a title the guild uses and she does not correct. It is not a claim about any goddess in particular, and everyone concerned prefers to leave it that way.

178.title: Gallery
178.content: Cured, and standing on eight legs about it. Llolth’s curse took her mind and her shape. The party gave the mind back, twice; the shape was never on offer.

179.title: Eldath
179.content: Goddess of still waters. Nobody’s patron. She came anyway. Eldath is one of the Oakfather’s daughters, and she is not on the list. Seven patrons came in dreams when the first Ley Crystal fell, and she was not among them. Then Sofia came out of the Far Realm breathing and did not wake up, and of everyone who might have been expected to arrive, the ones who actually did were the daughters. | Mielikki came to the grove.
