She did not enter, did not speak, and wept. | The Oakfather did not come at all. | Eldath asked permission to sit with her once a week. Then she picked Sofia up and carried her to LIMA herself. | . That is the entire measure of her. A goddess of still water, asking a room full of exhausted mortals whether it would be all right if she came back on a schedule, and then quietly solving the logistics problem nobody had the hours to solve. She comes once a week. She sits. She does not try to wake her.

180.title: The argument at the bedside
180.content: The other thing she has done is refuse to accept it. Steven walked into the ward at LIMA and found two goddesses arguing at whisper volume over Sofia’s bed — Eldath and Essyliss, disagreeing about method. Their working idea is a forced wildshape, and neither of them will promise it brings her mind back. No decision has been made. Both goddesses were clear that this one is not theirs to make. The party gets the vote, and Steven owes them the conversation. Where she stands now. In a chair beside a bed at LIMA, once a week, arguing with a serpent goddess about whether a thing that has never been undone can be undone. Seven patrons were handed out. This is the eighth god in the group, and she was not assigned to anyone.

181.title: Emma Wip
181.content: Paladin of Gond. Ruler of Wip. Dead for years, and still giving orders. Emma Wip was a paladin of Gond and the ruler of the city that carries her family’s name — a sword mage who drew power straight out of the heart of The Rock, the way her family always had. The motto is carved into half the masonry in the capital and it was not decoration: Strong As The Rock. Priscilla Adhmad, Ramses’s bastard daughter and one of Baz’s company, loved her, and died in Wip in the same hour she did. There were other Wips once — a family that held the offices of a city between them and expected to go on doing it. The war and the years took them. And Emma herself was killed by the shapeshifter wearing Catroniel’s face, before the timeline ever split: murdered by a thing wearing the face of a friend, which is a sentence this campaign keeps having to write. Her face went on ruling. R4 took her plate, her circlet and her voice, and has held the throne of Wip in them ever since — through a siege, an alliance, a war council and a regency. Every treaty the Council of United Members has signed was signed by a dead woman’s hand. Nobody has ever needed to explain to the city why the Queen looks tired, or why she is often away. Wip has been at war for most of her reign. The strangest thing about the arrangement is how little of it anyone has had to invent. Where she stands now. Gone, and unreplaced — a family emptied of heirs and a crown that nobody living has a legitimate claim to. What is left of Emma Wip is a suit of armor on a warforged, a motto on a wall, and a city that has never been told.

182.title: Essyliss
182.content: Goddess of Devotion. Patron of Steven. Binding force of the World Serpent. Essyliss is the goddess of devotion, Steven’s patron, and — as the party learned at the Dragonsmoot, in the middle of Steven publicly defending her — a member of the World Serpent. Not merely a member: the binding force. The nine can stand in the same place and still not cohere into the Serpent without her. That is why IO wants her found, and why the party was sent to do it. The strategy is hers. Find a way to silence the Siren’s Song; gather mortal forces and weapons; make Ghroth retreat; then follow him into the Far Realm on the Primordial Shadows and end him there, because the gods cannot enter that place. What went wrong between them. She was critically wounded at the Edge of Existence — the far rim of the Astral Plane, where the planes run out — looking for intel on Mappo No Ryujin. When Steven broke his vegetarian tenet under the Craving, the meat-hunger Ghroth’s bite left in him, he surrendered the Everscale to her and lost his boons with it. Then she stopped answering — to Steven, to Thoth, to any divine means at all. Where she stands now. She was folding blankets at LIMA HQ under the name Sienna, while Bahamut searched the planes for her. Steven found her. They reconciled. She gave the Everscale back, wrote a new tenet of her own — “I will not give up” — and agreed to help. She had gone and looked at Mappo No Ryujin herself, and concluded the war was hopeless. Steven told her about Innominandum. She changed her mind. She has not yet gone to the Outlands, and she is currently arguing with Eldath over how to heal Sofia.

183.title: Gallery
183.content: The goddess of devotion and her prophet, back when the boons still answered. How it is drawn. How it actually went: an aid-house, a false name, a tenth tenet apiece, and the Everscale handed back.

184.title: The Faces of Farylse
184.content: Gloom, Regret, Shatter. Not everything guarding the doors of the time-plane was a monster. Some of it had been people. Farylse does not name its door-keepers after who they were. It names them after what is left. Every one of them made a deal — with Damian Heath, or with Astridia — and now they keep the doors they bargained for.

185.title: Gloom
185.content: General Gloom was the immortal general of the City of the Palanquin. When Ghroth came, he did the largest, bravest, most competent thing anyone in this campaign has ever done: he went to the Land of Gears for help, woke the Palanquin titans, and carried an entire city and its armies out of Ghroth’s path. He carried them to Farylse. And then he watched all of it turn into the other things on this page. Astridia offered to numb the pain if he would guard her portal. He took it. The party left with his Captain’s Seal and a letter, to be shown to his younger self — early enough that the Palanquin and its neighbors can be rallied instead of evacuated.

186.title: Regret
186.content: Regret is Farylse’s name for Captain Jhodos Rumoxath, a triton pirate king who gave everything to save his crew and lost them anyway, and has never once put it down. He taught the party to ride the time-terrain — which is the skill that let them bank decades of Farylse time, and therefore the reason R4 had seventy years to spend on Marvin’s seal and Asfache had fifteen to spend on a griffon. He gave them his Star-Shell Pendant, to be shown to his younger self at Pirate Isle to rally the tritons. The Amulet of the Planes misfired mid-con and dropped Una, R4 and Steven directly onto Pirate Isle. Nobody knocked. The pendant stayed in the pack. It is still there.

187.title: Shatter
187.content: Shatter is what became of the gear-people’s souls: caught in time and still working. Each one of them is many of them at once, and they have never stopped digging.

188.title: Gallery
188.content: Regret. The triton who never put it down. Shatter. Many at once, still digging. The Mad Queen of Albion was also met on Farylse, and she is a door-keeper of the same kind — see her own page — the Albion portal is hers.

189.title: Flamencio
189.content: An Artist. Where the White Lion writes things into existence, Flamencio paints them. Flamencio is one of The Artists, and he is by a very wide margin the friendliest thing in that category. The party met him on Ancient Gamble Island, after Freya threw them backwards through time — he was dealing blackjack out of a shack on a mostly barren island, and appeared delighted to have customers. That is also where the party first laid eyes on the Chronologians, who turned up looking for exactly the sort of disturbance the party had just made. Getting home cost them a bribe, and part of the bribe was the rights to Asfache’s smoothie business, which Flamencio won and has never given back. He gave them a painting of an ear to summon him with. Later, at Thoril’s tavern, he painted each of them a small four-by-six that works as a portal — “I’d LOVE to paint you all” — and he meant it more literally than anybody was ready for. Because when they needed the White Lion, Flamencio put them inside his own canvases. The Lion Who Shakes the Spear lives outside space and time and cannot be walked to. A painting can go where a road cannot. That is how the party reached the being who wrote the writ that silences the Siren Song — through paint. Where he stands now. Under Allies on the ledger: an Artist with no stake in this war who keeps helping anyway, out of what appears to be pure professional enthusiasm.

190.title: Freya
190.content: Goddess of Magic. Patron of Una’s aspect; Smolder’s tentative patron. Freya is the goddess of magic, and the only patron the party has physically rescued. The Chronologians took her when the party jumped back in time, and the party fought their way through a Chronologian stronghold alongside Mordenkainen to get her out. Damian Heath released them both together. Una carries an aspect of her, one of the things she put down at the Far Realm threshold and picked back up on the other side. Smolder is a tentative champion. Where she stands now. At the Edge of Existence with Thoth and Kratos, waiting for Thoril to call.

191.title: Gallery
191.content: Released. The only patron the party has ever had to go and physically fetch.

194.title: Rat
194.content: Rat . Bloodthirst. A vorpal longsword with opinions, a taste in creature-types, and no interest in being sheathed. Rat, as the dice see him. *“Rat with Malacus?” — a misheard Arch Devil, immortalized.* . *Immune to crit. Two Champions of the gods, receiving the news.* . *“OH MY GAWD!” The master thief, being carried out of somewhere by a cleric.* . Rat and the Witness, in the Beastlands. Nothing in his hands at all.

195.title: R4
195.content: R4 . R4, wearing Emma Wip’s face — the Queen of Wip — standing over his own sabotaged teleport circle while Ragar reads it.

196.title: Ralf
196.content: Ralf . Ralf before: a dwarf, a hammer, and exactly one personality. Then Etheniss’s sabotage killed him in the Soul of the Rock, and what walked back out was an igloid body, a fistful of Ley Crystal shards — and the same hat. Ralf. Six minds, one hat, and the Ley Crystals showing through where his eyes used to be. The same wizard, a different one of him. The table has opinions about which.

197.title: Smolder
197.content: Smolder . Catman. A secret identity in the sense that everybody knows and nobody says it out loud. The robe of eyes, worn on the high street like it is nothing. Twenty percent off for the nearsighted, today only. The robe and the sword together. Between them, something is always watching, and something is always hungry. Bloodthirst got what it asked for. Smolder is still working out how he feels about how easy that was. Before the empire, before the Underdark, before the franchise: a monk, a road, and no accounts to keep. Freya’s tentative champion, doing a very convincing impression of someone who meant to end up here. Shrubby. The table has agreed not to discuss Shrubby. Smolder, with hair. The Smut Shaq’s grooming division has range. What the table calls the Hulk. What Smolder calls a productive afternoon in a difficult market. Scale is a matter of perspective, and Smolder’s perspective has always been expensive. Diplomacy, Smolder-style: acquire the assets first, negotiate the terms at leisure. Nala and Raja. The White Lion wanted his severed pieces back. He paid in a fresh writ and these two, who now manage Smut Shaq locations.

198.title: Asfache
198.content: Asfache . Asfache and Rodney, back when Rodney was still a fledgling and an afternoon in Farylse had not yet aged him fifteen years. The Land of Elements. He united the fire clans, took the Field of Fire, and had a drink about it. *“You get an orange, you get an orange!” — the Champion of War, distributing morale.* . A franchise. Of course it is a franchise. *“Ya bolstered with smoothies!” Support, as practiced by the god of war’s own.* . *“Ya bolstered!” The whole party has heard this. Most of them were bleeding at the time.* . The Feywild, First Run. A tarrasque took the leg. The artist’s version is smaller and no less pleased with itself. The replacement, First Run: in the field, out of what was lying about. It held. Steven did the fitting, First Run. Neither of them stopped to ask whether it was a good idea. Asfache, as the dice see him. Asfache and Kratos. It has never been a subtle relationship. Pentad-Nine rides on his back and answers to him. Nobody has satisfactorily explained why. Corpse-duty in Limbo: one modron, one warrior, and the githzerai who had been watching them for rather too long.

199.title: Una
199.content: Una . “I let my hair cover my other eye, for drama.” . The scales came in gradually, and then all at once. Dracogenesis. The Breath of Becoming: her father’s fire, Kereska’s magic, and the company that got her there. Una and Oman over the Djermani Hills — the audience she spent a year earning. The Field of Fire at Viavolca Way refused her mortal shape. It had no objection at all to the other one. *“Your mom is a baddie.” Steven, being Steven.* .

200.title: Steven
200.content: Steven . The Prophet of Essyliss. The hat is not, as far as anyone can establish, doctrinal. *Lizard, Laugh, Love. Nine of the ten tenets are spoken. This one he had inked.* . “I need to speak to the mayor.”* **New Dwarf City. The mayor was a shapeshifter, and his remaining tenure was measured in minutes.* . Having removed the incumbent, he did consider the vacancy. LIMA came out of it instead. LIMA on the march. The rank ladder runs Lizard, Alligator, Dragon, Grand Lizard, and the sending stones mean it runs without him. Going up the wall the direct way, as is his custom. Farylse. A Chronologian, and Steven’s foot, arriving at the same place at the same time. The afternoon the party learned that Steven has a type. Essyliss and her prophet, back when the boons still answered. Devotion, drawn the way devotion is usually drawn. The real version involved an aid-house, a false name, and a very long argument. “Anyway, I’m covered in bones.” There was more to the sentence. Nobody remembers it.

201.title: Bram
201.content: Bram . Bram Balls. Same-plane teleport charms, distributed liberally. Do not ask. The other one in the room. He plays facing the crowd. There is a reason for that, and the crowd has never once noticed it.

202.title: Sofia
202.content: Sofia . *“I’MA DROP THAT WALL!” — the battle druid’s entire tactical doctrine, in four words.* . The wall in question. The brain in question. The green orb came out of one of these. The Oakfather, imparting wisdom. He has not come to the grove since. Sofia and the elder brain. The green orb came out of one of these.

204.content: Thoth . The table’s contribution to Thoth scholarship. The god of knowledge has declined to comment.

205.title: Aditi

207.title: Freya
207.content: Freya . Released. The only patron the party has ever had to go and physically fetch.

210.content: Väinämöinen . Giving directions. A god with no voice, explaining who took it. Bram got there in the end.

213.title: Damian Heath
213.content: Damian Heath . The offer. He had nothing to lose by letting them try, and he has never once looked worried about the answer.

222.title: Mappo No Ryujin

226.content: IO (Asgorath) . Every dragon in creation, holding perfectly still, listening to a plan that cannot currently be done.

227.title: Tiamat
227.content: Tiamat . The handover in Limbo. She got exactly what she was promised, and left believing the rest.

236.title: Catroniel
236.content: Catroniel . Before Gamble Island. Two hands, two legs, and a con that had run five weeks without incident.

245.title: Dryzzlazz
245.content: Dryzzlazz . Cured, and standing on eight legs about it. Llolth’s curse took her mind and her shape. The party gave the mind back, twice; the shape was never on offer.

246.title: Heart Melts

They killed him — and the Orb of Consciousness shattered with him, which is why the igloid army woke up with minds of its own, and why nobody has found Cal since. One of his war machines. Newport built to a scale nobody else on the continent was building to, and this is what the party was expected to stand in front of.

247.content: Thoril . Marvin’s seal, whole. Ninety seconds, almost no noise, and half a life.

254.content: Malachas . Two weeks and one minute.

264.content: 2.2 · The Road to Wip . Safe passage, priced in souls. Ralf paid double and has never explained why. The underground river. Smolder kept one as a hat. The Giddyup Saloon. Alissa looked into the mirror, and was gone.

268.content: 2.6 · The Primordial and the Time Cops . One strand, cut on purpose. Everything that went wrong afterwards is downstream of it.

270.title: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear
270.content: 2.8 · Truth, and the Lion Who Shakes the Spear . Tap a forehead, see a shapeshifter. A continent’s worth of paranoia, solved by poking people.

272.title: 2.10 · The Amulet and the Edge
272.content: 2.10 · The Amulet and the Edge . In, around every guardian, and out with the amulet. Almost clean. The road to the Edge of Existence. Everyone on it had been told how the odds ran. Five years of work, one sheet of paper, and it did exactly what it said on the day.

273.title: 3 · Farylse & the Chronologians
273.content: 3 · Farylse & the Chronologians . The Land of Gears — a city on turning cog-plates, and the home the Unnumbered were cut loose from. Not everything in Farylse wanted to teach them anything. The spider queen, for one. And the Void, which is a place, and also — occasionally, and unpleasantly — a thing that comes out of it.

274.title: 4 · The Second Run Begins
274.content: 4 · The Second Run Begins . “This way for good times.” The arm was still wearing Catroniel’s ring. The Lizard of the Opera. The title role is played by an actual lizard, and the reviews were extraordinary.

275.content: A solved problem, and a new liability riding in a sack. Asfache fishing Rat back out of the fluid. Nobody has ever said what the fluid was.

276.content: 6 · The Dragonsmoot . The first assembly of dragonkind in ten thousand years, and nobody had thought about the seating.

277.content: 7 · The Dying Feywild . Five roots down in the first round. The sixth is the one the whole plane hangs on. A week ago these were the most beautiful things in creation.

278.title: 8 · Seventy-One Hours
278.content: 8 · Seventy-One Hours . Everything divine, left on the grass. They walked in as themselves and nothing else. Beautiful, and running on gears. She was hanging in the middle of it with her eyes open. Somewhere with no light in it at all: the Sunless Lake.

279.title: 9 · Chaos in Wip
279.content: 9 · Chaos in Wip . The Hearring call, before anyone had finished waking up. The Everscale changes hands. The whole city heard the question.

280.title: 10 · The Late Radtismir
280.content: 10 · The Late Radtismir . The exhale. A down payment, not a pardon. Mordenkainen builds a body; Carxi is having a lovely time. The leg is the part that sells it. The most dangerous object in the cosmos, treated as a receipt. Dozens of students, one set of instincts, and Ralf taking notes through all of it.

281.title: Ghroth’s Forces
281.content: A wall of Ley Crystals once sealed reality away from the Far Realm. The wall is failing. Ghroth the Siren waits behind it with a horde and a song that, sung uncontested, opens the door for everything hungry behind him. Ahead of him come the Three Lieutenants, each stripping a plane to feed him. One of them is dead. Two are not. Ghroth — The Siren. Magnum Innominandum — First Lieutenant. Dead. Magnum Tenebrosum — Second Lieutenant. ~30 hours. Mappo No Ryujin — Third Lieutenant. Waiting. Nyarlathotep — Freed by mistake. Beaten twice. Never gone. Nephren-Ka — Wore a friend’s face. Driven off twice.

283.title: Ghroth
283.content: The Siren. The thing on the other side of the wall. A wall of Ley Crystals once sealed reality away from the Far Realm. The wall is failing, and Ghroth is what waits behind it — with a horde, and with a song. The Siren Song is the weapon. Sung uncontested, it opens the door for everything hungry behind him. Raw, rolling across an assembled army, it mutates soldiers and heroes alike: Steven’s teeth, Asfache’s eyes, the frog sac it planted in Sofia’s throat and left there for years before switching it on. The party has fought him. At the end of the First Run they destroyed the last Ley Crystal themselves to force him to arrive early and on their terms. He came, at the Edge of Existence, and the song began, and Steven raised the writ and silenced it. It worked. It was not enough. The Three Lieutenants descended, the line broke, and the battle went the way the most rational minds in the cosmos had always said it would. The party wound the world back and started again. Where things stand. The win condition is already in the party’s pack: reach the Edge with every force that will come, and when Ghroth opens his mouth, read the writ. The army is the remaining problem — and so is everything below.

284.title: The Gods
284.content: When the Jun Ley Crystal shattered and the wall around reality lost a stone, the gods came calling — in dreams. Each member of the party was given a divine patron and a mission, and the long work of the Five-Year Prep began. The patrons are not distant. Thoth tore the party out of the Dragonsmoot mid-sentence. Freya was a prisoner the party had to break out of a Chronologian cell. Kratos was above the Feywild canopy swinging at a Lieutenant while the party worked its roots. Essyliss stopped answering anyone at all, and turned up under an assumed name folding blankets in Steven’s own headquarters. Seven patrons were handed out across the party. Eldath was not one of them and came anyway. Thoth — Knowledge — Rat . Aditi — Consciousness — R4 . Kratos — War — Asfache . Freya — Magic — Una, Smolder . Essyliss — Devotion — Steven . The Oakfather — Nature — Sofia . Väinämöinen — Yore — Bram . Eldath — Still waters — nobody’s patron, Sofia’s visitor .

285.title: Heart Melts
285.content: Clockwork dragon. Ruler of Newport. The one who broke the wall. Heart Melts was a clockwork dragon and the ruler of Newport, and he is the reason there is a clock on any of this. His army was the igloids — clockwork drones by the thousand, run through his Orb of Consciousness — and they were the force that ringed Wip in the siege the party walked into on their first day in the city. His family held the commands: Pyre, Prodigy, and Perception Melts. Then he went to Jun. He came down through the roof of the temple, into the ziggurat beneath it, and destroyed the Jun Ley Crystal — one of the stones in the wall the gods built between the world and the Far Realm. Aberrations poured through the gap. King Ramses survived it, gravely wounded. Only the Wip crystal was left, with roughly five years in it, and the doomsday clock started that afternoon. He also took Cal, pulled into the Orb of Consciousness. The party killed him at the Battle of the Jun Ziggurat. The Orb shattered with him — which freed the igloid army into minds of its own, and left Cal’s fate unknown. When the party jumped back five years, they landed after that fight: Heart Melts is dead in both runs, and nothing they have done since has had to account for him. What is left of him is the family and the city. Newport is an ally now — trade restored, the siege a piece of old history — and the Melts sit inside R4’s Council of United Members, allied by necessity and old arithmetic.

286.title: Gallery
286.content: The Battle of the Jun Ziggurat. Six people, a temple floor with a hole in it, and the thing that had just come down through it. They killed him — and the Orb of Consciousness shattered with him, which is why the igloid army woke up with minds of its own, and why nobody has found Cal since. One of his war machines. Newport built to a scale nobody else on the continent was building to, and this is what the party was expected to stand in front of.

289.title: La Bomba
289.content: The magic missile bomb. Three steps: build a receptacle, channel magic missiles into it, set it off.

290.title: 1 · Creating the receptacle
290.content: Time: construction takes 25 days, reduced by the Arcana score of each character actively working. If someone stops working, their Arcana score is added back to the days remaining. Example: Ralf (6), Una (3), and Ragar (7) working together take 16 days off the total — 9 days of all-day construction and incantation. Construction: each day, everyone working rolls Arcana and adds the results together. Collectively beat DC 30 and a day is subtracted from the total. Fail, and roll a mishap (1d100). Receptacle: one pound of material, shaped into an orb and prepped with runes. The material sets the maximum missiles it can hold: . | Material | Max missiles | . | Copper | 3 | . | Silver | 6 | . | Iron | 12 | . | Steel | 24 | . | Electrum | 27 | . | Gold | 54 | . | Mithral | 60 | . | Platinum | 72 | . | Precious gems | 105 | .

291.title: 2 · Channeling missiles into the receptacle
291.content: You must be able to cast magic missile to fill a receptacle. Adding a cast takes 2 hours per spell level — or spend 24 hours and hit a DC 18 Arcana check to add all of your spell slots for the day (the “All Day Add”; fail the check and you only add slots up to 4th level). Broken concentration on a single add: the missiles are not added and the slot is expended. Broken concentration during an All Day Add: you lose half your spell slots, your choice of levels. Blast radius: 10-ft radius once the bomb holds 10 missiles, +10 ft per additional 10 missiles. Range: 120 ft, +10 ft per 10 missiles.

292.title: 3 · Casting La Bomba
292.content: The caster must be holding the orb and must be able to cast a 1st-level spell — you do not need to know magic missile to set one off. The caster spends 1 action concentrating per 10 missiles (minimum 1 round) and may do nothing else — no movement, no bonus action, no reaction — or the spell fails. If concentration breaks, the cast fails but the bomb is not spent. When the count is done, the release must come immediately (within 6 seconds) or the working collapses. After casting, the receptacle is expended. Example: a fully filled gold receptacle (54 missiles) takes 5 turns of pure concentration; on the 6th turn, Una casts La Bomba — 54d4+54 force in a 50-ft radius, at up to 170 ft. There are no timers and no fuses. A La Bomba goes off because somebody stood still in the middle of everything, long enough to finish. For what the party is currently carrying, see the Armory section of The War Ledger.

296.title: The First Run
296.content: Five years of preparation. One catastrophic mistake. A battle they lost. With one Ley Crystal gone and the last one counting down, the gods came calling — in dreams. Each member of the party received a divine patron and a mission, and the long work of the Five-Year Prep began. They got three years and three seasons of it. Not five.

297.title: What it was
297.content: It was a campaign of alliances and arsenals. The party forged pacts city by city, crafted La Bombas by the crate, gathered divine followers, and hunted the shapeshifters who had quietly infiltrated every continent. They cured Dryzzlazz of the curse that had driven her mad and tried — clumsily — to broker peace with the Drow. They recruited the ancient golden dragon Meiko to scour the world for more of her kind. They also went places nobody sane goes. Into a dead lich’s tower to steal a piece of divinity out of a table. Into a mind flayer city to free a primordial and get a goddess arrested for it. Into a dwarven kingdom drowned in shadow to wake a god who had stopped caring. Into a painting, to rob a being that lives outside space and time. And they solved the hardest problem of all: the Siren Song itself. Bram’s search led him to Väinämöinen, a god who had lost his voice to the White Lion. Guided by the Artist Flamencio — who painted the party directly into his canvases to reach a being outside creation — they confronted the Lion and pressed him into creating a writ to silence the Siren Song. Then they took it by force, hacked the Lion apart, and fled with the one object that might actually win the war. They did nearly everything right.

298.title: How it ended
298.content: In the Fall of Year 3, Rat slipped into Tiamat’s tomb in Avernus and made off with the Amulet of Null. He carried it back to the mortal plane, and Null the Dragon God was freed — and the divine line holding the Edge of Existence came apart from behind. So the party made a desperate gamble. They destroyed the last Ley Crystal themselves, forcing Ghroth to arrive early and on their terms rather than his. The Siren Song rolled over the assembled army and mutated it, and then Steven raised the writ and silenced it. It worked. It wasn’t enough. The Three Lieutenants descended, the line broke, and the battle went the way the most rational minds in the cosmos had always said it would. So they reached for the one option left: a Time Travel Scroll, looted from a maze two years earlier by people who had no idea what they were saving it for.

310.title: After After World
310.content: “The gods built a wall of crystal to keep the dark out. The crystals are cracking. Someone needs to hold the line — or find a way to sing louder than the thing on the other side.” . A wall of Ley Crystals once sealed our reality away from the Far Realm and the Great Old Ones beyond it. The wall is failing. Ghroth the Siren waits on the far side with a horde and a song that, if sung uncontested, opens the door for everything hungry behind it. A band of unlikely heroes failed to stop that song once. Then they turned back time — and now they are living the years over again, armed with the memory of how it all goes wrong. This site is the chronicle of that campaign: the story so far, and the running quest log.

314.title: Magnum Innominandum
314.content: First Lieutenant. Dead — the first ever to fall. Innominandum came to drain the Feywild through Marvin’s Seal: a massive, gnarled tree-entity feeding on a plane through six great roots. Freya, Kratos and Thoril fought it directly above the canopy and could not kill it while it fed. Cutting it off from the seal was the party’s job. All six roots were severed. It dropped onto the seal, raised a titan out of the beauty it had stolen, and was driven off anyway. It fled to the Far Realm, and the party followed on fragments of Primordial Shadow. How it died. Rather than lose, it tore the governor out of its own engine to detonate the realm. Asfache spotted the tendrils still trailing off the ruined controls. R4 stood there holding the Amulet of the Planes, with an exit in his hand, and declined to use it. The whole party took hold and became the governor together — six creatures that are not deterministic, choosing the same limit at the same moment, with a way out available and refused. Innominandum materialized inside its own works, and Smolder and Rat killed it there. The first of Ghroth’s three Lieutenants, and the first ever to fall. There is no other successful defense against Ghroth on record, anywhere, ever. What it cost. Sofia, used as the relay and pulled out too late to save who she was. Horus and Nubia, spent permanently. Half of Thoril, with the other half already owed to Callahan’s door. And seventy years of R4’s Farylse time, poured into the seal so the Feywild would come back whole. A grey circle two hundred feet across is all that’s left where it rooted. The fey call it The Silence.

316.title: IO (Asgorath)
316.content: Progenitor of dragonkind. One of the nine. He called every dragon in creation to a field, and then he was the only one left standing in it. IO — Asgorath — is the progenitor of dragonkind and a member of the World Serpent, the nine-fold entity that was once whole and has not been for a very long time. He fragmented, and the fragments are Bahamut, Tiamat and Null. He called the Dragonsmoot, the first in ten thousand years. Every dragon alive heard the summons: a raspy, straining voice, like someone trying to speak through a broken instrument, because the force that should have made it whole was missing.

317.title: What he said in the field
317.content: His arrival stopped a brawl the size of a continent — and triggered the Dracogenesis that had been building in Una for years. It stalled her between forms, and it was Kereska who named the rite that could finish it and Oman who breathed the fire. IO watched the whole thing happen. Then he declared his purpose to the assembly: remake the World Serpent. Which requires the binding force, Essyliss, who was not there — and requires Null, who is sealed in an amulet that had already been quietly stolen out of Tiamat’s horde. He told every dragon present, out loud, that he intends to free Null. He also stepped between Tiamat and the party when she caught the scent of the shadow mark and came across the field. Then he charged the party with a task — find Essyliss and bring her to the Outlands — and began to say something further about Null. He never finished the sentence. Thoth reached across the planes and pulled the party into the dying Feywild mid-word. Every other dragon in that field heard the rest of it.

318.title: The empty field
318.content: When R4 and Una came back to the Outlands with a sending stone for Oman, the Dragonsmoot was over. No dragons. No serpent gods. Only IO, alone, in the field he had filled. He took the stone. He said nothing about where anyone had gone — that the party learned hours later, from Tiamat, on a rooftop in Wip: he had sent her after Null, and Bahamut after Essyliss. Where he stands now. In an empty field, one sending away. R4 has its pair in his pocket, and nobody has reached for it. The party is quietly working against his stated plan, and he does not appear to know it.

320.title: The Junish Company
320.content: Baz’s people, who outlived him. Two clerics, a bodyguard, and two spies who taught Rat a trick. One of them died before the timeline split. Willamet Adhmad and Priscilla Adhmad are half-elf clerics, half-siblings to Baz Stricknaz, and, like him, bastard children of King Ramses Jun. They came to Saki with their brother’s private army and wanted no part of the ritual he was planning there. They asked the party for help stopping it. The party stopped it. At the Battle of Saki, Willamet dragged Baz out of the fight and healed him three times. Bram killed Baz while Willamet was trying a fourth. Willamet hated him for it, badly enough that his god went quiet on him for a while. Una, Asfache and Bram talked him round on the only argument that mattered: Newport could be beaten without killing orphans. He healed everyone and came with them. Priscilla arrived after the dust settled, with the six Junish soldiers who were left. She asked everyone, one at a time, whether they were committed to saving Jun. She got a yes. Mark is Willamet’s bodyguard. Where Willamet goes, Mark goes. That is the whole entry, and it has never once been wrong. Blade, a tabaxi, and Silrael, an elf, were Baz’s spies. They tried to recruit the party for him in Saki (Silrael spoke exactly once, to say they had to go), and then sat out the ritual, because the Junish thieves’ guild does not tamper with fiends and they are guild first. They joined the road to Wip. On it, Willamet and Priscilla taught Smolder, Ralf and Bram a spell apiece; Blade and Silrael taught Rat how to hurt people who were not looking. Wip. The company split to get into the occupied city. Priscilla, Blade and Silrael were flown in invisibly to find the Thieves Guild. Willamet, Mark and the soldiers went to Moongate and were captured by the Cantines, who meant to trade Willamet to Newport for their kidnapped matriarch, Luna Cantine. Priscilla walked into the Underground Arena, stopped a drider from setting her spiders on the party with three words (“Those are my fighters!”), put Asfache up as her champion, pleaded against the trade of her brother, and paid half of a ten-thousand-gold deal to get the party to the harbor. The party rescued Luna before the trade could happen, and Skoll Cantine gave Willamet back. Her teleport ring is what took the party to Jun. She loved Emma Wip. She died in the chaos of the imposter’s ambush in Wip, in the same hour Emma did, at Smolder’s hands. That was before the timeline ever split, so she is dead in both runs. Mopak. For the Battle of Jun the party teleported Willamet and his company to Mopak instead. On purpose. He took it well: he rebuilt the town to a thriving point, refused to trade with Newport, and at one stage had to be sent a firmly worded message by R4 to stop attacking Newport ships. Mopak is in the alliance because of him, and it is in the alliance the same way in the Second Run. Baz raised a private army on forged royal writs. The part of it that survived him is the part that was never really his: two clerics who wanted the ritual stopped, a bodyguard who only ever answered to one of them, and two rogues who answered to a guild. Where they stand now. Willamet and his company hold Mopak, allied, still not trading with Newport. Priscilla is buried in Wip.

321.title: Kereska
321.content: Dragon goddess of magic. One of Una’s two patrons. The one who knew what the old rite was called. Kereska is the dragon goddess of magic, and her fingerprints are on two of the most important things that have happened to this party — neither of which she made much noise about. The first was a direction, and she never gave it out loud. When the Jun Ley Crystal fell and the question became how long the Wip crystal could be made to last, it was in researching Kereska that Una turned up Meiko herself — an ancient gold at the base of Mont Kiara who might know how to extend a crystal’s life. Everything downstream of that meeting, including Una’s entire relationship with dragonkind, starts with a name found while reading about a goddess. The second was a rite. At the Dragonsmoot, Una’s Dracogenesis stalled halfway: triggered by IO’s arrival, then stuck, with a woman hanging between two forms in front of every dragon alive and nobody in the field knowing what to do about it. Kereska knew. She named the Breath of Becoming — an ancient working in which a dragon of the subject’s own lineage breathes fire upon her to forge the change — and then did the half of it that is not fire. Oman loosed his flame; Kereska wove draconic magic through it; and Una walked out of the burning as a young golden dragon. Where she stands now. Unaccounted for. When R4 and Una went back to the Outlands, the field was empty of everyone: not Bahamut, not Tiamat, not the serpent god Merrshaulk, not Meiko, not Oman, and not Kereska. Only IO was left in it. She remains one of Una’s two patrons — Freya holds the aspect, Kereska holds the guidance — and of the two, she is the one who has never once explained herself.

322.title: King Ramses Jun
322.content: Elected King of Jun. Bearer of the Staff of Isis. The man who sealed the door. Ramses Jun is the elected king of Jun, which is a distinction the Junish take seriously and the rest of the world keeps forgetting. The Crown of Jun is not inherited and cannot be taken: it has to be freely given by the ruler before, and everything else about the office follows from that one rule. He carries the Staff of Isis, and it is not ceremonial. The staff raises barriers — and one of those barriers is the reason the Far Realm portal in Jun’s temple is a sealed door rather than an open one. He also holds the kingdom’s seven Healing Stones, which turn a hard night into a long rest for anyone standing near them; on a war footing they are worth an army’s weight in clerics. He has paid for all of it. Heart Melts put him on the floor of the Jun Ziggurat, gravely wounded, in the fight that destroyed the Jun Ley Crystal — and the sight of the king going down is what sent Baz’s reaper-shadow completely insane in a room that was already collapsing. His family is a war on its own terms. Bast, Horus and Nubia, the monks of Jun, are his siblings — two of them now permanently spent. Baz Stricknaz is his bastard son, and the last thing Baz did alive was raise a private army on forged royal writs. Willamet and Priscilla Adhmad, his other two bastards, are the reason that army ended up on the party’s side. He is also, in the least dramatic and most useful way, the reason anyone knows what the world looks like. The map the party carries was commissioned by Ramses from the mapmaker Tingle, copied off the king’s own map table. Where he stands now. On the ledger, under Allies — a wounded king with a staff that closes doors, in a kingdom that has already lost its crystal and lent the party its airships.

323.title: Kratos
323.content: God of War. Patron of Asfache. Kratos is the war god, and Asfache is his Champion. It is not a subtle relationship. He fights on the line personally. During the battle for the Feywild, Kratos, Freya and Thoril were above the canopy going at Innominandum directly, while the party worked the roots below — the gods could not kill it while it was feeding, and cutting it off from the seal was the mortals’ job. Where he stands now. Back at the Edge of Existence with Thoth and Freya, waiting on Thoril’s call.

325.title: Luna Cantine
325.content: Matriarch of the Cantines. Head of the Wolves. Intermediary Queen of Wip. Luna Cantine is the matriarch of an extensive lycanthrope family who prefer the word okami, the head of the Wolves — one of the three houses of Wip’s Thieves Guild — and the ruler of Moongate. The party got her out of besieged Wip early in the First Run, which is a debt she has never mentioned and never forgotten, and shortly afterwards she made Asfache a lycanthrope for the asking. Everything since has been the long game. The Cantines went from a criminal family with an interest in city politics, to a family with seats at the table, to the family sitting in the chair at the head of it — and nobody can point to the moment it happened. She came to R4 on the morning he was leaving the plane. Not summoned, not sent for: she simply arrived, on the correct morning, at the correct hour, in front of the one person who had a throne he could not sit on and a war he could not miss. She asked for nothing. She walked out intermediary Queen of Wip. The same day, in the War Room on The Rock, she stood up in front of the small council and told them the crater in the harbor district — the one left by a La Bomba — was the work of Far Realm creatures. Nobody contradicted her. Including the Queen. She is also the one who turned to Smolder and asked whether he would answer the next message out of Mont Kiara, when Ulaxium had gone quiet and six strange people had started writing in his place, all of them asking for “best friend.” He said he would. That thread opened on him because she put it there. Her son Skol is a story in himself. R4 sent him to answer a distress call from the Arcane University with seven La Bombas in his hands, and Skol went silent, and stayed silent, and Luna spent a winter being told to wait. He came home free as part of the deal struck at Mont Kiara — and then the two of them organized the training of the largest army the world had assembled in living memory. Where she stands now. Running a city whose Queen is on another plane, without a proclamation, a ceremony or a raised voice. The war ledger files her under It’s Complicated, which is fair. She has done the party nothing but favors, she has never once named a price, and she does not strike anyone as a woman who forgets a number.

326.title: The Mad Queen of Albion
326.content: Encountered in Farylse. Not a Chronologian — but she is standing in the doorway. Beyond Damian’s stronghold, out on the broken temporal plane of Farylse, the party found a crazed, long-haired woman in a crown, endlessly guarding a portal that led nowhere anyone could name. She was one of several strange things met there and, at the time, one of the least urgent. She is now standing between the party and the Shadowfell. What is known. The way in to the Sunless Lake — where Tenebrosum is feeding on Callahan — runs through Albion, on Mystica. The Mad Queen of Albion guards that portal, and does not remember why. She is the same crowned woman from Farylse. Nothing else about her has been explained: not how she got from a shattered time-plane to a kingdom on Mystica, not what the portal was for, not what she has forgotten. Somebody did eventually manage a likeness — from a long way off, and from behind. She did not turn around. She was watching the road.

327.title: Malachas
327.content: Arch Devil. Freed twice. Punctual. Malachas was found behind a door inside HIS Tower, imprisoned, and the party let him out in exchange for two weeks of truthful answers. He gave them, and he gave them straight — including the answer to the puzzle room that the table has never once let go of: .

328.title: “Bing bongabong boing boop boop boop.”
328.content: He also told Rat something nobody else was in a position to know: that Caspian had seized the Nine Hells after the Blood War ended, and that he would like some help doing something about it. Then he left a contact stone, which appeared in Rat’s workshop precisely two weeks and one minute later, exactly as advertised. Arch Devils are punctual. In the Second Run the party freed him again — which is the only reason Avernus was ever reachable at all. And then the stone finally got used. He did not need persuading, did not haggle, and did not ask what had changed. He brought forces, he brought intelligence, and he found the target: Caspian, aboard Zariel’s old flagship, over Avernus. The party joined his host and the assault began. Nobody has asked the obvious question out loud. When Caspian falls, Avernus has a vacancy — and the party is currently helping to create it, in the company of an Arch Devil who has been extremely helpful, entirely honest, and never once surprised.

330.title: Mappo No Ryujin
330.content: Third Lieutenant. Coiled around the Pool of Memories, and anchored there. Mappo No Ryujin is the least understood of the three. It is on the Astral Plane, coiled around the Pool of Memories — Ohn’s memory storage, the thing Asfache dreams about and can now watch shrinking. Two people have gone and looked at it, and both paid for it. Essyliss went herself, searching for intel, and it very nearly killed her. She was critically wounded over it at the Edge of Existence, the far rim of the Astral Plane, where the planes run out — and she drew a conclusion from what she saw: that the fight against Ghroth was hopeless. She has since changed her mind — but she is the only living being who has looked at Mappo with her own eyes and walked away. Sofia paid for the rest, as the Lieutenants’ relay, and the single most useful thing she brought back is this: Mappo cannot leave the Pool. It is anchored there. Which means the party chooses the moment. Of the three Lieutenants, this is the only one that is not on a clock — and the only one where the party gets to pick the ground, the hour, and the state they arrive in.

331.title: Gallery
331.content: The Pool, and what is drinking it. Asfache sees this most nights. It is smaller every time.

332.title: Maps
332.content: The world as the party has seen it drawn — from the table’s first hand-inked continent to the charts of a world mostly still in silhouette. Contents . | The Known World | The Home Archipelago | Junkweil, Hand-Drawn | Wip, the Capital | Mystica | Topoda | The Land of Yore | The Land of Elements | The Pirate Isles | State of the World | .

333.title: The Known World
333.content: The poster edition, and the best single picture of the world there is: Topoda in the northwest, Mystica across the middle sea, the home archipelago off to the northeast, and the southern continents — Caelum, Unda, Fax, Ignotus, Brevis — that Asfache spent five years walking. Inset panels for Gaiadon and the Pirate Isles, which sit far to the south. The little land marked FARYLE out in the Mortem Ocean is spelled the way the mapmaker heard it. The world as the party knows it — commissioned by King Ramses from the mapmaker Tingle, derived from the map table in Jun. Everything in silhouette is still out there. The same world to scale. The campaign began on the little cluster in the upper right. The same map with the GM’s pen on it, for anyone who has lost track: T is Topoda, M is Mystica, LoE the Land of Elements, Yore and Eara are themselves, the blue circle is home, and the red circle is the Pirate Isles. A high-resolution version of the world map lives here on Google Drive.

334.title: The Home Archipelago
334.content: Junkweil and its neighbors: Onkro, Tamsend, Gaiadon, Newport, and the volcano isle of Sanddown.

335.title: Junkweil, Hand-Drawn
335.content: The original table map of Junkweil — Lake Junkweil to the Forbidden Jungle, with the Riverway and the Two Kings Road. Pirate Isle is the one with the skull.

336.title: Wip, the Capital
336.content: Wip’s districts — Cleargate, The Rock, The Harbor, Westgate, Fishsong, Ghostforge, Moongate, Glassplace — and the sewer lines under them, which have mattered more than once. The citadel under The Rock: from the War Room down through the Underwell to the Mines.

337.title: Mystica
337.content: The Second Run abroad: Albion, Gaul, Djermani, Istria, Kemet — and the road the party traveled from Albion down to Tyre. The Kemet reach: Alexandria, Lycopolis, Crocodilopolis, Thebes, and the river between. The same continent drawn by nation and by weather — Albion in red, Gaul in green, Istria in purple, Hellas in orange, Kemet in blue along its river. Hot in the west, cold in the east, and the Isle of the Tempest sitting offshore in weather of its own.

338.title: Topoda
338.content: All of Topoda, named: the Kitami Tundra and Warnhome Pass in the north, the Protected Lands in the middle, the Ethereal Wastes and Q’dar in the south, the Land of Gears across the water — and the Neverfog on the western edge, which is exactly as helpful as it sounds. That coast up close: Treetop Town, Ana’s Wood, and Weresharks Grotto — where the whole story started, before the clock did.

339.title: The Land of Yore
339.content: The Land of Yore: Glarsht, Bram’s family home, on the Sovth River.

340.title: The Land of Elements
340.content: The Land of Elements as it was first charted, before the party finished exploring it: Viavolca Way, the Volcarun Hills — and the Edge of Existence.

341.title: The Pirate Isles
341.content: A small scatter of islands in the southern ocean, south of the Land of Elements and a very long way from home — harbours, camps, a mine, a volcano, and one skull. Nobody has written the names in. Jhodos Rumoxath’s younger self is somewhere on them, and the aboleths are somewhere in the water around them.

342.title: State of the World
342.content: The Year 1 status map, with the key: religion marks for the Oakfather, Freya, and Essyliss; stability dots — green thriving, orange stable, red unstable, black unknown. Two later snapshots of the same tracking — note the green dot at Wip, and the red one at Jun. Jun knows what a broken crystal costs.

343.title: Marvin
343.content: One of the three who killed Orcus. He has been the Feywild’s front door ever since. Marvin killed a demon prince with his friends and then spent the rest of forever repairing the damage. He, Thoril and Callahan slew Orcus, and the killing weakened the bonds between the Material Plane, the Feywild and the Shadowfell. Marvin sealed his own soul into the Feywild to hold it; Callahan did the same for the Shadowfell. For a very long time it worked, and nobody thought about him. Then Innominandum came and put six grey roots down onto a dome of golden light and began drinking the Feywild through him. Inside the dome, when the party finally got close enough to look, his spirit was flickering — tired, fading, still holding. R4 poured seventy years of his own Farylse time into that seal. Not to win the fight; to make sure that what was left afterwards was worth resealing. It worked past anybody’s expectation. The seal came out of the fight not cracked, not scarred, not leaking. Whole. Because of those seventy years, Marvin got something almost nobody in this war gets: a last lucid conversation with a friend, before he settled permanently and finally into the seal he has been for centuries. And the Feywild that came through unscarred is the reason Aquandria pledged every fey court, without conditions — the largest alliance win of the Second Run. Where he stands now. He is the door. He always was. The difference is that this time somebody paid for it in front of him, and he was awake to see it.

344.title: Meiko
344.content: Ancient gold dragon of Mont Kiara. Una’s mentor. Went looking for an army and has not come back. Meiko is an ancient gold dragon who lives at the base of Mont Kiara, beneath the Arcane University. The party’s first-ever business with her was a hostage negotiation, and it was one of their own doing the holding: in the First Run, Ralf had her captive up the mountain. The deal that freed her was three-cornered — gems for the wizard, freedom for the dragon, and Skol Cantine walked out in the same bargain, which was the answer to a question Luna had been asking for a year. Then Una gave her the egg back. That is the moment the whole relationship turns on. The egg had been out of Meiko’s keeping, and Una returned it, and in exchange Meiko told her what had been happening to her body for years: Dracogenesis. She was becoming a dragon. Meiko asked one thing in return, and Una promised it: if Meiko dies at the Edge of Existence, Una looks after the egg.

345.title: The second time around
345.content: In the Second Run Una went straight to the mountain, and the two of them were allies from the first conversation. They flew west together to the Djermani Hills and found Oman — Una’s father — waiting in a bigger lair than the one he had left. Then Meiko went recruiting. Somebody has to persuade the rest of dragonkind to stand at the Edge of Existence when the time comes, and an ancient gold who is owed favors across half a continent is the right somebody. Where she stands now. Unknown. The Dragonsmoot dispersed and took her with it, and Oman with it too. Nobody has seen either gold since, and nobody has said where either of them went. The egg was still safe when the party last left Mont Kiara, which is not nothing, given what has been happening up that mountain.

346.title: Cal & Memory-Cal
346.content: One of them is missing. The other one is not really him, and Asfache knows it. Cal was taken by Heart Melts’ Orb of Consciousness at the Battle of the Jun Ziggurat. The party killed Heart Melts, the Orb was destroyed in the same fight, and what happened to Cal has never been established. He sits on the ledger under Missing & Unreachable with no line of inquiry attached to him. Memory-Cal is a different thing, and everybody is clear about that. He is Asfache’s memory of Cal, made walking and warm by a droplet of the Pool of Memories — the green orb Asfache carries. He is not a ghost, not a resurrection, and not a lie. He is exactly what he looks like: a man remembering his friend, hard enough that the friend is standing there. He dissolves when the orb is left behind. And at the threshold of the Far Realm, that is precisely what had to happen. Asfache put the orb down, because nothing of the Pool could be carried in, and watched Cal come apart in front of him for the second time in his life — knowingly, deliberately, with the fight still ahead of him — and walked in anyway. He reforms when the orb is picked back up. That does not make the moment on the threshold cheaper. It makes it a thing Asfache has now chosen twice. If a single droplet of the Pool can do this — build a whole person out of one man’s memory of him — then the question of what the entire Pool could do, in the wrong hands, is not a small one. It is currently being drunk by something. Where they stand now. Cal: unknown. Memory-Cal: wherever the orb is.

348.title: Bast, Horus & Nubia
348.content: The Monks of Jun. Three siblings who lend a willing host their hands. Two of them have been spent. The Monks of Jun are siblings of King Ramses Jun, and they do not fight for you so much as fight from you. A monk temporarily possesses a willing host under a tenancy agreement with two terms, and the terms are the whole of their theology: .

349.title: Do good. Protect your family.
349.content: Sign that, and the monk moves in, and the host can throw Junish Strikes — a flurry that is not theirs, delivered by hands that are. | King Ramses Jun — first born. On the throne, not in the tenancy. | Bast — second born. Soft, slow, wise. | Horus — third born. Loud and straightforward. | Nubia — fourth born. Harsh and intelligent. | . They have been in the party’s corner since Jun’s temple, where they recognized Nephren-Ka’s true form under the face she was wearing and fought beside Smolder to drive her out of it.

350.title: What it costs
350.content: There is a second thing a tenant can do, and it is not a flurry. It is the Junish Sacrifice: the monk spends themselves, entirely and permanently, to buy the host something the host cannot otherwise have. Smolder spent two of them in the Far Realm. Nubia went first. Then, deeper in — inside the runaway engine, with the plane coming apart around six people who had chosen to hold it — Horus volunteered, and went too. They are not resting. They are not elsewhere. They are gone, and their strikes went with them. Where they stand now. Only Bast remains — one brother, one strike, and no further relief valve. He is soft and slow and wise, and he knows exactly what he is for. Nobody on the public muster rolls counts this as a casualty. It is two.

352.title: Mordenkainen
352.content: Archmage. Consultant. Presumably charging by the hour. Mordenkainen entered this story the way most things enter it — sideways, through a devil. In the First Run, Rat took Ralf and Malachas down to the Nine Hells to speak with him, and the working relationship has survived a timeline reset, a heist, a funeral and a war. In the Second Run he has been in Avernus with the Amulet of Null and a spellbook written by his own future self, working on a doorway into the Null Realm — a place where nothing exists, and therefore a place Ghroth cannot eat. An escape hatch, built by a man who does not appear to believe in escape hatches for other people. Then the party asked him for a corpse. He built one: Rat, to the last scar, cold on a slab — and grafted on the real severed leg, so that Tiamat’s own tracking would confirm the kill for her. Carxi heard the plan and grinned. It worked perfectly. And then he read the circles. His diagnosis is the single most useful sentence anybody has produced about the party’s transport problem, and it is not a good one: every teleport circle on the continent delivers to Avernus, and it is a trap that was built for this party. He can repair it. The price he quoted is about a year of his work, without Alamil. Where he stands now. He teleported the party to the war and he is standing in it with them, over Avernus, alongside Carxi. Which makes the most expensive man in the cosmos the party’s ride home. Nobody has established what any of this is costing. He has never once mentioned a fee, which is somehow more alarming than an invoice.

353.title: Nala & Raja
353.content: Two leonin, acquired in a body-parts trade, currently running a chain of adult entertainment venues. Nala and Raja came into the party’s service as part of a settlement. In Farylse, the White Lion wanted his severed body parts back; the party wanted a fresh writ to silence the Siren Song; and somewhere in the negotiation two leonin were added to the party’s side of the ledger. Nobody has ever recorded what they thought of this. They have since become one of the most quietly useful assets the party owns. They manage the Smut Shaq locations — Nala in Wip, Raja in Jun — which is not the joke it sounds like. A chain of busy, popular houses in two capitals is income, it is morale, and above all it is intelligence: people talk in them, constantly, and two leonin who work for the party are always in the room. Nala handles the combat end of the arrangement. Raja handles the stealth end. Between them they cover most of what a franchise in a war zone actually requires. With the Catty Shack leveled — R4 dropped a La Bomba on it because Smolder was annoyed about the competition — the Wip market is now entirely uncontested. Nala’s quarterly figures have never looked better. Where they stand now. Listed together under Allies on the ledger, holding the party’s civilian empire together in two cities while everybody who owns it is on another plane.

355.title: Nephren-Ka
355.content: Wore a friend’s face in a lich’s library. Driven off twice. Killed neither time. Nephren-Ka is a shapeshifting servant of Ghroth, and the party stood next to her for an entire afternoon without knowing it. In the First Run, at the bottom of HIS Tower, they reached the library they had been sent for and found Prodigy Melts already in it, studying a mystical orb suspended over a runed table. She was researching how to wake the inert warforged, she said, and the key to it was whatever was sealed inside the orb. They had been dealing with shapeshifters all year. They were suspicious of her. They discussed it. And then they let her carry on. What came out of the orb was Nyarlathotep. Ink flooded the room, replicas of the party rose out of it — and Prodigy dropped the face she was wearing. The party fought their own shadows, a shapeshifter horde, and Nephren-Ka herself, in the one room in the world where Thoth’s power could not reach them. They won the room. They did not get her. She retreated into the Far Realm and left the trace of a portal behind her. They spent the rest of that day trying to force the portal open and could not. The next morning she opened it herself and walked back in — and was driven off into the Far Realm a second time. Thoth’s rule, given the same day, has held ever since: “The more powerful of Ghroth’s ilk will travel to the Far Realms to escape danger. They almost always strike again.” . In this run, the orb in HIS Tower has never been opened. Rat holds the tower with a crew of tinkers, the library is undisturbed, and nobody has gone down to check whether anyone is standing in it.

356.title: Null
356.content: The third dragon god. Sealed in an amulet. Released once, by this party, with results. Null is the third of IO’s extensions, alongside Bahamut and Tiamat, and the only one of the three who is not at large. He is sealed in an amulet, and he has been for a very long time.

357.title: The worst decision anybody made
357.content: . In the Fall of Year 3 of the First Run, Rat slipped into Tiamat’s tomb in Avernus and stole the amulet. He carried it back to the mortal plane, and Null came out. What followed was ruin. Null tore loose on a revenge rampage against his own siblings, killed gods, and destabilized the divine line holding at the Edge of Existence at the exact moment that line could least afford it. Mordenkainen had quietly intended to use the amulet — to carve a refuge out of the Null Realm, or to ransom it to Bahamut. Every one of those plans ended in the same hour. It is the single worst decision anyone in the party has ever made, and undoing it was one of the first things they did with their second chance.

358.title: This time
358.content: In the Second Run, Carxi was dispatched to retrieve the amulet before Rat’s first-run self could ever bring it to the mortal plane. It went to Mordenkainen, who began working it into an escape route. At the Dragonsmoot, IO noticed the amulet was gone — and then began to say something about Null, and never finished it, because Thoth pulled the party out of the assembly mid-sentence. Every dragon at that gathering heard the rest of the sentence. The party did not.

359.title: Where the amulet is now
359.content: With Tiamat. The party handed the real amulet over off a counterfeit corpse in Limbo, as the price of a dragon queen’s departure. So Null’s prison now rides with the sister who helped seal him, on the errand of the father whose intentions toward it nobody in the party has actually heard. The party is the only faction alive that has watched an unsealed Null end a war.

360.title: Nyarlathotep
360.content: Encountered in various forms. Freed by mistake. Beaten twice. Never gone. Nyarlathotep is the Far Realm thing the party let out themselves. In the First Run, deep in HIS Tower, the party found a woman calling herself Prodigy Melts in the library, researching how to reactivate the warforged. The key, she said, was whatever was held in the orb. She was Nephren-Ka in disguise, and the orb held Nyarlathotep. The party let her carry on, and the orb came open. Nephren-Ka fled to the Far Realm; the party fought shadow versions of themselves on the way out; and something that wears many shapes was loose in the world. It met them again in the Dwarven Mountains, when they reached Dwarf City shrouded in darkness: it greeted them, fought them, and escaped to the Far Realm once more. In the spring of Year 3 the party trained an army for it and beat it in both realms, mortal and Far, in the same campaign. That was the First Run. In this run, the orb in HIS Tower has never been opened. Rat holds the tower now, with a crew of tinkers. Nyarlathotep is wherever it was before the party ever arrived. It is not one of the Three Lieutenants, and it does not feed on a plane. It is older than that arrangement, and it serves nobody’s schedule but its own.

361.title: The Oakfather
361.content: God of Nature. Patron of Sofia. The Oakfather is Sofia’s patron. His daughters — Eldath, Mielikki and Shiallia — gave her the seeds. Under his patronage Sofia built the travel-tree network the party’s armies move through and began raising an Ent Army. What happened after. When Sofia came out of Innominandum alive and no longer herself, Mielikki came to the grove, stopped at the edge, said nothing, and wept. Eldath asked permission to sit with her once a week, and later carried her to LIMA HQ herself; she is now one of the two goddesses arguing over how to bring her back. The Oakfather did not come. The Ent Army is decaying — bark off-color, sap running blue, the awakened trees gone silent.

362.title: Gallery
362.content: The Oakfather and Sofia, in better years. He did not come.

363.title: Ohn, in the Doll
363.content: The forgotten god of memory. Five miles of clay for a body, a doll for a home, and no idea who he is. Ohn is the forgotten god of memory, and he is forgotten on purpose. He is sealed inside a clay titan five miles tall, carved all over, raised once out of the Susini Sea — and he has no recollection of being a god, a titan, or anything else. The party met him inside the titan in Farylse, learned to work the thing, and then watched the whole structure begin to come apart when they left. Una used Divinity Transfer — the spell she brought back from Farylse that moves divine essence between beings — to save what was inside it, and what was inside it now lives in a doll. In Sylvania he woke up a little. Asfache was dreaming of a silver lake in the astral void, and the doll started moving on its own, and when the party finally put the doll and the green orb together the god in the doll recognized it instantly: .

364.title: “That’s mine — it will help me… remember.”
364.content: What he has now is awareness, not memory. He knows the titan at the bottom of the sea is his body. He knows there is a Pool somewhere with the rest of him in it. And he knows, with a cheerfulness that makes it much worse, that something is drinking from it: .

365.title: “Something is eating me. I can feel it. I’m getting smaller.”
365.content: He cannot lead them there. Not yet. A god of memory with no memories does not know the road. He has to be put back in his body first — and his body is still at the bottom of the Susini Sea, in a world where nobody ever went and got it. Where he stands now. In a bag, in a doll, cheerful, curious, fond of puzzles, and running out of himself.

366.title: Gallery
366.content: The body. Five miles of it. The Susini Sea, in the run where somebody went and looked.

367.title: Oman
367.content: Ancient gold dragon. Una’s father. The fire she was forged in — and, at present, an empty space where a father used to be. Oman is an ancient gold dragon and Una’s biological father. He went west, years ago, for a bigger lair — which is a perfectly ordinary reason for a dragon to leave and a considerably less satisfying one for a daughter — and Una and Meiko found him in the Djermani Hills in the Second Run, together.

368.title: The Breath of Becoming
368.content: At the Dragonsmoot, IO’s arrival triggered Una’s Dracogenesis and then stranded it: she hung between forms, neither woman nor dragon, and could not finish the change. Kereska recognized the rite. It requires a dragon of the subject’s own lineage to breathe fire on her — and there was exactly one dragon of Una’s lineage standing in that field. Oman loosed his full flame on his daughter. Kereska wove magic through it. Una came out of the fire a young golden dragon, forged in her father’s breath, in front of every dragon in creation. It is the defining moment of the assembly, and it is also the last time anyone has seen him.

369.title: The unfinished gift
369.content: Una was pulled out of the Outlands mid-audience — Thoth does not wait — and the thing that has bothered her ever since is not the interruption but the arithmetic of it: she has a father, and no reliable way to reach him. So back in Wip she took one of her own golden scales to a magic item maker and commissioned a communication device out of it, for him. It is still on a workbench, unfinished. Where he stands now. Gone. When R4 and Una returned to the Outlands the field was empty and IO was standing in it alone. R4 left the god a sending stone to pass along to Oman if he finds him. Which makes the scale on that workbench the only line to her father that Una actually controls. Oman is one of the six dragons who could recognize Rat on sight — and one of the four who would never mention it to Tiamat.

370.title: Allies, Rivals & Others
370.content: Not the party, not their patrons, not the thing behind the wall — everyone else the war has put in the room. A god keeping a bar. A rakshasa who has been watching for two years. An archmage who is also the ride home. A piece of grey weather that will not leave. Thoril — Killed Orcus. Spending himself in halves. Caspian — Took Avernus. Currently under fire. Mordenkainen — Built the corpse. Named the trap. The ride home. Marvin — The Feywild’s seal. Whole, and gone. Callahan — The Shadowfell’s seal. The clock is him. The Cat Lord & Felina — Gave the verdict. Gave the bell. The Witness — Watches Rat. Says nothing. Decides everything. Carxi — Rat’s protégé. Died once, professionally. Malachas — Arch Devil. Freed twice. Punctual. The White Lion — Wrote the writ. Twice. Under protest. Flamencio — The Artist who paints the door. Baz Stricknaz — Died at Saki. Still following Bram. Rodney — Fifteen years in an afternoon. Dak’kon — Caught watching. Asked for help. Nala & Raja — Traded for body parts. Run the franchise. Ohn, in the Doll — The forgotten god. Getting smaller. Cal & Memory-Cal — One missing. One remembered. The Faces of Farylse — Gloom, Regret, Shatter. Dryzzlazz — The Spider Queen. Cured twice. Pentad-Nine — The modron that changed its mind. Heart Melts — The clockwork dragon who broke the Jun crystal.

372.title: The Party
372.content: Nine adventurers who washed ashore at Saki half-drowned, spent five years preparing for the end of the world, lost that fight at the Edge of Existence, and wound time back to do it again with foreknowledge. They are now the only faction in creation that has killed one of Ghroth’s Lieutenants. Rat — Champion of Thoth. Officially dead. R4 — Champion of Aditi. Rules Wip behind a borrowed face. Ralf — Six minds, one metal body. La Bomba. Smolder — Smut Shaq, the Underdark, and Catman. Asfache — Champion of Kratos. Seer of the Pool. Una — Young golden dragon. Dracogenesis. Steven — Prophet of Essyliss. Holds the writ. Bram — Bard of Yore. The one who killed a prince. Sofia — The Ent Mother. Retired.

373.title: Pentad-Nine
373.content: A Mechanus pentadrone. The engine’s limiter. The only thing in creation that has looked at the proof and said no. Pentad-Nine — P-9 — was the governor of Innominandum’s engine: a modron of pure law, torn out of its seat by the Lieutenant and fed into the gears to make the machine run without a limit. It survived that. Then it watched six creatures who are not supposed to be predictable take hold of the governor themselves, together, with an exit in one of their hands that they declined to use, and choose the limit. Its conclusion is arithmetic, not sentiment: the event occurred, therefore it was possible, therefore the model that excluded it is incomplete, therefore the proof is incomplete.

374.title: Why that sentence matters
374.content: Mechanus ran the pattern on Ghroth and concluded the end is inevitable — and a plane of pure law does with the inevitable what law does: it stopped resisting and began administering it. Primus accepted a proof submitted from outside the plane, and Mechanus opened a conduit feeding lawful order into the Far Realm. Modrons walk into it in an orderly queue, because they were told to and the instruction was lawful. P-9 was one of them. It no longer accepts the proof. It is attached to the party until it can find somebody with the standing to hear it say so.

375.title: Working with it
375.content: It rides on Asfache’s back and answers to him. It is never wrong, it is never kind, and it never volunteers anything — which is why nobody knew, for a long while, that it had been holding the Lieutenants’ schedule the entire time. When someone finally thought to ask, it answered instantly: seventy-one hours until Tenebrosum finished Callahan. It knows when. It does not know why, and it says so. Where it stands now. On Asfache’s back, wherever Asfache is — still refusing the proof, still waiting for somebody with the standing to hear it say so. Riding out of the Far Realm on the one who chooses hardest.

377.title: Prime Quest
377.content: Location: The Edge of Existence . Status: Active (endgame) . Objective: Gather forces and silence the Siren Song at the Edge of Existence — the incomprehensible frontline where the gods battle Ghroth’s forces. The Strategy (per Essyliss): Find a way to silence the Siren’s Song. Gather mortal forces and weapons to use against Ghroth. If/when they can make Ghroth retreat, use the Primordial Shadows to follow him into the Far Realm. Allied mortal forces will pursue Ghroth there and end him for good — because the gods cannot enter the Far Realm. Intel: The party visited the Edge — the far rim of the Astral Plane, where the planes run out — in the First Run. R4 later took the Gaiadon delegation there for perspective. Essyliss was critically wounded there searching for intel on Mappo No Ryujin. Ghroth had three known Lieutenants: . | Innominandum — dead. Killed in the Far Realm. The first ever to fall. | Tenebrosum — Shadowfell, at the Sunless Lake, feeding at double rate since Innominandum died. ~30 hours until it finishes Callahan. | Mappo No Ryujin — Astral Plane, coiled around the Pool of Memories, and anchored there. It cannot leave. The party chooses the moment. | . Relation: MS-01 (Silence the Siren), MS-02 (the Alliance), MS-03 (the Arsenal).

379.title: ✅ MS-01: Silence the Siren — Writ Secured
379.content: Source: Essyliss (via Steven), Väinämöinen (via Bram) . Objective: Ensure the party can counter Ghroth’s Siren Song at the Edge of Existence. In the First Run, Bram found Väinämöinen, who had lost his voice to the White Lion. Flamencio (an Artist) revealed the Lion’s nature and painted the party into paintings to reach him. The party persuaded the White Lion to create a writ to silence the Siren Song, then ambushed him and seized it. Steven used the writ in the final battle — it worked, but they lost anyway. In Farylse, the party met the Lion again (Artists cannot be conventionally destroyed) and traded back his severed body parts for a new writ plus two leonin followers, Nala and Raja. Status: The party has the writ going into Round 2 — the win condition is secured. It must be used right before Ghroth appears, so the mortal forces aren’t mutated by the song as they were in the First Run.

380.title: ⌛ MS-02: The Alliance
380.content: Status: Active — significantly progressed . Objective: Unite the factions of the world against the Far Realm. The party has been forging a continental coalition city by city to field a combined force at the Edge of Existence. R4 and the Council of United Members coordinate from Wip. The alliance now spans Junkweil, the dwarven holds of Onkro, the minotaur nation of Gaiadon, Newport, and the Drow of the Underdark. Major campaigns remain in progress in the Land of Elements and Mystica, and several Farylse contacts offer untapped alliances. See the sub-quests below.

Objective: Build weapons capable of harming Far Realm entities at scale. | MS-03a — La Bombas: Ragar manufacturing at scale; plans shared with the Arcane University; Ley Crystal shards hold 900 missiles (precious gems hold 105).
